q [parameter] — Injection rate value of 4 m3/day.
p0 [parameter] — Initial pressure value of 100 bar.
sigma0 [parameter] — Initial stress value of -100 bar.

Water Production [process] — A physical process of extracting water from the reservoir.<SEP>Water production is a process simulated in the 3D heterogeneous saline aquifer using the reservoir simulator GEM.

Hydrodynamic Model [technology] — A method used to simulate the flow of fluid in the reservoir.<SEP>A model that simulates the physical processes of fluid flow.<SEP>A model describing the permeabilities of the damage zone and fault core.

Vertical Displacement [parameter] — The measurable quantity of vertical displacement in the coordinate interval 𝑟≤500 m.<SEP>A measurable quantity related to the movement of a point in the vertical direction.<SEP>A measurable quantity representing the vertical movement of the rock formation.
Radial Stress [parameter] — The measurable quantity of radial stress in the coordinate interval 𝑟≤500 m.<SEP>A measurable quantity related to the stress in a radial direction.
Vertical Stress [parameter] — The measurable quantity of vertical stress in the coordinate interval 𝑟≤500 m.
Hydro-Geomechanical Model [technology] — A coupled model based on MUFITS and FLAC3D for hydro-geomechanical simulation.
Transient Fluid Flow [process] — The physical process of fluid flow to a vertical well in the numerical experiment.

Aquifer [geologicalbody] — A geological body capable of storing and transmitting water.<SEP>A layer of rock capable of storing water that is the target for CO2 injection.<SEP>A subsurface geological formation that contains and transmits groundwater.<SEP>A layer of rock or sediment that contains and transmits groundwater.<SEP>A subsurface geologic formation that can contain or transmit groundwater.<SEP>The subsurface rock fo
MUFITS+FLAC3D [technology] — A method or model for coupled hydro-geomechanical modeling.
Synthetic Model [technology] — A synthetic model constructed for two-dimensional multilayered formation to interpret calculations.

Undesired Mechanical Processes [process] — Mechanical processes including slip along the fault plane, crack opening on asperities, plastic deformations in the fault zone, target aquifer, and caprock, which are not desired during CO2 injection.
Overlying Collector [geologicalbody] — The geological body that collects CO2 leakage along the fault zone.

Multilayered Reservoir Structure [geologicalbody] — A multilayered reservoir structure with plane layers typical of aquifers located at a flat terrain.<SEP>A reservoir with plane layers typical of aquifers located at a flat terrain.
Depleted Gas Reservoir [geologicalbody] — A depleted gas reservoir with a pronounced structural trap formed by a caprock.<SEP>A gas reservoir with a pronounced structural trap formed by a caprock.

Injection Well [geologicalbody] — An injection well is a well used for injecting carbon dioxide (CO2) into the subsurface, specifically targeting a storage aquifer or reservoir. These wells are utilized for the purpose of injecting CO2 at varying rates depending on the individual well's characteristics. Typically, injection wells are vertical and play a crucial role in the process of subsurface fluid injection, which can be CO2. T

Basement Layers [geologicalbody] — Three low permeable layers each of 150 m height surrounding the target aquifer.<SEP>The rock layers below the target aquifer, which are also affected by the increase in pore pressure.<SEP>The layers located beneath the target aquifer.

Damage Zone [geologicalbody] — Damage Zone refers to the area around the fault core where rock fractures are denser and more active, influenced by fault parameters such as slip, length, and displacement. It is characterized by natural fractures and high levels of deformation. Specifically, it is a relatively narrow zone of large deformations surrounded by the transitional zone of fractured rock, often with a thickness of 1 mete

Basal Aquifer [geologicalbody] — The aquifer placed below the caprock and basement layers.<SEP>A basal aquifer is a layer of rock or sediment that lies below the main aquifer and can serve as a potential storage or transmission layer.<SEP>A layer of rock below the main aquifer.

Perforation Interval [geologicalbody] — The intervals through which CO2 is injected into the target aquifer, located at depths of -910 to -890 m and -1910 to -1890 m.<SEP>A segment of the wellbore where perforations have been made to allow fluid flow.<SEP>A specific part of the upper aquifer where perforations are made for CO2 injection.<SEP>An interval near the upper aquifer where plastic deformations and similar domains are observed.<

Injector [wellborecomponent] — The well coinciding with the left border of the reservoir, used for CO2 injection.<SEP>The injector is a well where CO2 is injected into the reservoir.<SEP>A well used for injecting carbon dioxide into the upper and lower aquifers.<SEP>A component used for injecting CO2 into the geological formation.
Pore Water Salinity [parameter] — The salinity of the water within the pores of the reservoir rock, which is neglected in the simulations.

Youngs Modulus [parameter] — A measure of the mechanical properties of the reservoir rock, represented by the Young’s modulus 𝐸.<SEP>A measurable quantity that describes the elastic properties of the rock affected by the injected fluids.<SEP>A measure of the stiffness of a material.
Poisson Ratio [parameter] — A measure of the mechanical properties of the reservoir rock, represented by the Poisson ratio 𝜈.

Cohesion [parameter] — A measure of the mechanical properties of the reservoir rock, represented by cohesion 𝑐.<SEP>A specific mechanical property of the storage aquifers and caprock.<SEP>Cohesive force between particles in the formation.

Angle of Internal Friction [parameter] — A measure of the mechanical properties of the reservoir rock, represented by the angle of internal friction 𝜃.<SEP>A specific mechanical property of the storage aquifers and caprock.
Heat Conductivity of Saturated Porous Medium [parameter] — The heat conductivity of the saturated porous medium, set to 3 W / (m ⋅K).

Fault (Damage Zone) [geologicalbody] — A fault is a fracture or zone of fractures between two blocks of rock. The damage zone refers to the region of a fault that is more susceptible to fracturing.<SEP>A zone of damage around the fault core.<SEP>A damage zone within a fault with a porosity of 0.1 and a permeability of 0.6 mD.
Fault (Core) [geologicalbody] — The main crack in the fault zone.<SEP>A core within a fault with a porosity of 0.1 and a permeability of 10^{-2} mD.
Synthetic Reservoir Model [other] — A model used to represent the reservoir for studies.<SEP>A model used as a reference for boundary conditions in the coupled model.

Host Rock [geologicalbody] — The rock surrounding the fault core with different mechanical properties such as elastic modules, cohesion, and internal friction angle.<SEP>The main rock matrix in which the fault core is embedded, differing in mechanical parameters.<SEP>The rock unit that forms the main body of the fault zone.<SEP>The host rock is the primary rock type that forms the background structure of the cells in the dama

FLAC3D Simulator [technology] — A numerical modeling software used for simulating the mechanical behavior of rock masses, particularly for CO2 injection studies.<SEP>A numerical simulator used for stress analysis and deformation modeling.

Pore Pressure Increment [parameter] — The increase in pressure within the pores of the geological formations.<SEP>The increase in pore pressure due to CO2 injection compared to the initial hydrostatic distribution.<SEP>The increase in pore pressure within the domain occupied by the CO2 plume.<SEP>Increase in pore pressure compared to the initial hydrostatic distribution.<SEP>The increase in pore pressure in the aquifers compared to th

Volumetric Strain [parameter] — The strain in the target aquifer due to CO2 injection and tectonic stresses.<SEP>The target aquifer exhibits large values of volumetric strain.<SEP>The change in volume of the domain occupied by the CO2 plume.<SEP>A measurable quantity, indicating the deformation of the rock formation in the fault zone.<SEP>The deformation of the rock caused by the injection of carbon dioxide.<SEP>Measure of defor

Caprock Layer [geologicalbody] — A layer of rock located at a depth in the target aquifer where significant volumetric strain and pore pressure are observed.<SEP>The layer of rock where the fault zone is located and CO2 leakage occurs.
Target Layer [geologicalbody] — The target layer is the part of the reservoir where CO2 spreads.
Temperature Effect [process] — The injected CO2 cools the reservoir in the vicinity of the injector.
Mechanical Equilibrium State [parameter] — The state of mechanical equilibrium of the formation during CO2 injection.
Pore Fluid Temperatures [parameter] — The temperature of the fluids in the pore space during CO2 injection.

Non-Isothermal Flow [process] — The flow of CO2 and pore fluids at different temperatures during injection.<SEP>Non-isothermal 1D steady-state pipeline flow equations are utilized in the modeling of gas transport networks, considering temperature changes along the pipeline.
Volumetric Strain Fields [parameter] — The strain fields observed in the formation during CO2 injection.<SEP>The strain fields in the aquifers at the end of the simulation period.
Coupled Hydro-Geomechanical Model [technology] — A model that combines hydrodynamic and geomechanical processes.<SEP>A model that couples hydrological and geomechanical processes.
Volumetric Deformation [parameter] — The change in volume of the rock due to stress.
Aquifers [geologicalbody] — Aquifer layers that store water in the reservoir.<SEP>Reservoirs where CO2 is stored.

Lower Aquifer [geologicalbody] — A lower layer of the aquifer that is part of the reservoir.<SEP>The lower layer of the aquifer where carbon dioxide is injected.<SEP>The lower layer of the aquifer system.<SEP>The lower aquifer is a type of geological body that is part of the storage system in CO2 injection processes.
Coupled Model [technology] — A model used to simulate the injection and behavior of carbon dioxide in the reservoir.
Lithostatic Pressure [parameter] — The pressure created by a layer of thickness 1350 m with a density 2400 kg/m3.
350 Bar [parameter] — The constant bottomhole pressure at which carbon dioxide is injected into the upper and lower aquifers.
30 Years [parameter] — The duration for which carbon dioxide is injected into the upper and lower aquifers.<SEP>The duration of active injection.

Pore Pressure Plume [process] — The distribution of increased pore pressure inside the domain occupied by the CO2 plume.<SEP>The distribution of pore pressure changes in the subsurface due to the injection of carbon dioxide.

Salt [material] — A material with a porosity of 0.01 and a permeability of 10^{-4} mD.<SEP>A general term for the precipitated minerals, including halite, used in the context of geological storage.<SEP>The mineral of Halite.<SEP>A chemical species, specifically halite, precipitated during the process.<SEP>The material forming the porous network in the porous media.
Salt Deposit [geologicalbody] — A rock unit in the formation, which is part of the lower part of the salt deposit.<SEP>A layer of salt rock or sediment.
Core of the Fault [geologicalbody] — The central part of the fault where the CO2 plume distributes partially.

Reservoir Thickness [parameter] — The vertical extent of the reservoir rock unit.<SEP>A measurable quantity that affects fault loading and reactivation.<SEP>The vertical extent of a reservoir.<SEP>The thickness of the reservoir complex in the simulation study.

Gas Saturation [parameter] — Measure of the amount of gas present in the rock.<SEP>The saturation of gas in the aquifers at the end of the simulation period.<SEP>Estimates of the level of gas (supercritical CO2) saturation in the domain, interpreted at the resolution of 4D seismic data.<SEP>The saturation of gas in the simulation, trained using FNO models.
Flow Properties [parameter] — Properties related to the flow of fluids in the rock.
Mechanical Characteristics [parameter] — The mechanical properties of the aquifers and caprock, which can be modified in the simulation.
Bulk Modulus [parameter] — A specific mechanical property of the storage aquifers and caprock.<SEP>A measurable quantity representing the resistance of the host rock to deformation.
Salt Layer [geologicalbody] — A type of storage aquifer.<SEP>A layer of the aquifer near the bottom part where plastic deformations and similar domains are observed.
Main Fracture [geologicalbody] — A primary fracture in the fault zone that does not open fully.<SEP>Primary fracture opening with a negligibly small aperture.
Fault Zone (Modified Model) [geologicalbody] — A fault zone with uniform permeability set to 10 mD, used in the modified model for CO2 injection simulations.
Transient Non-Isothermal Multiphase Flow [process] — The flow of a multiphase fluid in a rock formation under varying temperature conditions.
Mechanical Equilibrium [process] — The state of a system where all mechanical forces are balanced.
Non-Isothermal Multiphase Flow [process] — A process involving the flow of multiple phases under non-isothermal conditions in a rock formation.
Fluid Saturations [parameter] — A measurable quantity indicating the amount of fluid occupying the pore space of the rock formation.
Vertical Well [wellborecomponent] — A well component fully penetrating the infinite-acting reservoir for the purpose of fluid extraction.<SEP>A well with a constant injection rate of 0.
Transient Flow [process] — A process involving the flow of slightly compressible fluid over time to a vertical well.
Stress Tensor Components [parameter] — A measurable quantity representing the stress in different directions within the rock formation.
Coupled MUFITS+FLAC3D Simulations [technology] — A combined simulation technique using MUFITS and FLAC3D technologies to model multiphase flow and reservoir mechanics.
Fault Permeability [parameter] — A measurable quantity describing the fault's ability to allow fluid flow, with increased values leading to significant CO2 injection.
Volumetric Deformations [process] — Increase in volumetric deformations leading to an increase in porosity and permeability.
Permeability of the Host Rock [parameter] — The measure of the ability of the host rock to allow fluid flow through it.
Permeability of the System of Natural Fractures in the Fault Zone [parameter] — The measure of the ability of the system of natural fractures in the fault zone to allow fluid flow through it.
Stratification [geologicalbody] — The stratification refers to the layers in the layered formation, where the permeability of each layer is important for the hydrodynamical model.

Plastic Volumetric Strain [parameter] — Plastic volumetric strain (𝜀𝑝) is a measurable quantity that indicates the amount of deformation that the rock can undergo under stress before returning to its original shape.
Cell Permeability [parameter] — The permeability of the rock in the vertical direction.
Total Permeability [parameter] — The permeability along the x and z-axis.<SEP>The measurable quantity of total permeability.
Damage Zone Permeability [parameter] — The permeability of the damage zone in the rock unit.
Fault Core Permeability [parameter] — The permeability of the fault core in the rock unit.

FLAC3D [technology] — FLAC3D, also known as a mechanical simulator, is a software tool used for numerical modeling of geomechanical processes. It is specifically designed to compute the mechanical equilibrium state of fluid-saturated formations, solving the geomechanical sub-problem through methods such as numerical experiments for hydro-geomechanical modeling. FLAC3D serves as a technology for addressing quasi-static

Pore Pressure [parameter] — Pore Pressure is a measurable quantity representing the pressure within the pores of a material, specifically in the context of rocks. It refers to the pressure exerted by a fluid in the pore space of the rock, which can be measured. These zones often play a critical role in tectonic activities and can affect the mechanical properties of the Earth's crust. The fault zone is a specific region of interest in studies, focusing on alterations in permeability due to slip and deformations. It is a z

It is intersected by a tectonic fault and is the focus of a CO2 injection study, located at 950m depth. The target aquifer is a primary storage layer for CO2 in the geological formation, with a thickness of 100 m, and is of interest for CO2 injection and studying

Upper Aquifer [geologicalbody] — The upper aquifer is a layer of rock or sediment located above the caprock and basement layers, serving as part of the storage system in CO2 injection processes. It is characterized as a geological body above the target aquifer, which can store or transmit fluids. Deformations and Stresses [UNKNOWN] — The FLAC3D Mechanical Simulator computes deformatons and stresses.
Porosity and Permeability Fields [UNKNOWN] — Deformations and stresses are used to update the porosity and permeability fields.

Effective Stress Tensor [UNKNOWN] — The effective stress tensor, 𝝈′, is defined as 𝝈 + 𝛼𝑃, where 𝝈 is the stress tensor and 𝑃 is the pore pressure.

Domain [UNKNOWN] — The pore pressure plume diffuses along a domain of 1 km length in horizontal direction.
600 bar [UNKNOWN] — Bottomhole pressure is set at 600 bar.
Rock Formation Beyond Fault Zone [UNKNOWN] — The permeability of the rock formation beyond the fault zone is considered undamaged and equal to that of the host rock.
Self-Enhancing Halite Growth [process] — A process that creates three-dimensional porous networks with 40±15% internal porosity during CO2 storage in saline aquifers.

Porous Networks [geologicalbody] — Three-dimensional porous structures created by halite precipitation during CO2 storage in saline aquifers.<SEP>Porous networks that generate capillary forces drawing brine toward precipitation sites, accelerating growth.

Capillary Suction [process] — A process where porous hydrophilic aggregates generate capillary suction, drawing brine films toward precipitation sites, which accelerates the growth of halite.<SEP>The process by which porous precipitates amplify capillary suction.
Porous Hydrophilic Aggregates [material] — Aggregates that form porous structures, facilitating the capillary suction and nucleation process of halite.

Brine Films [material] — Films of brine that are drawn towards precipitation sites by capillary suction, contributing to the growth of halite.<SEP>The films of brine stabilizing on hydrophilic substrates at the microscale.

Positive Feedback Loop [process] — A feedback mechanism where the growth of halite accelerates due to the preferential nucleation at gas-liquid interfaces and the subsequent capillary suction of brine films.

Macrocrystalline Cores [material] — Dense cores of macrocrystalline halite formed under moderate supersaturation and evaporation during the two-stage precipitation process.<SEP>Refers to the dense centers of halite aggregates.

Microcrystalline Overgrowths [material] — Overgrowths of microcrystalline halite that form umbrella-like crusts, encapsulating residual brine beneath surface layers during the late-stage dynamics of halite precipitation.<SEP>Microcrystalline overgrowths from rapid late-stage dynamics that create umbrella-like crusts encapsulating residual brine.<SEP>Refers to the overgrowths on the macrocrystalline cores of halite aggregates.

Permeability Decline [risk] — A risk associated with the reduction in permeability caused by the formation of porous networks and the preferential obstruction of flow percolation pathways by halite precipitation.
Crystalline Cores [material] — Crystalline cores formed under moderate supersaturation and evaporation, surrounded by microcrystalline overgrowths from rapid late-stage dynamics.

Porous Architecture [parameter] — The porous architecture that explains why modest porosity reduction causes severe permeability decline, as aggregates preferentially obstruct flow percolation pathways rather than uniformly cementing grains or filling pore space.

Capillary-Driven Solute Delivery [process] — A mechanism that drives self-enhancing growth across nano- to centimeter scales, involving interface nucleation, secondary porous structure formation, steep concentration gradients, hydrophilic substrate film maintenance, and capillary-driven solute delivery.

Steep Concentration Gradients [process] — A mechanism that drives self-enhancing growth across nano- to centimeter scales, involving interface nucleation, secondary porous structure formation, steep concentration gradients, hydrophilic substrate film maintenance, and capillary-driven solute delivery.<SEP>Steep concentration gradients at evaporation fronts. Evaporation creates concentration gradients that peak at the drying interface and d

Porosity Reduction [parameter] — The reduction in porosity that causes severe permeability decline, as porous aggregates preferentially obstruct flow-controlling throats at gas-liquid interfaces rather than uniformly filling pore space or grain surfaces.

Pore Space [geologicalbody] — Pore space refers to the internal spaces within rocks and materials, particularly in the context of porous media. These spaces can be found between grains or aggregates, where flow percolation pathways are obstructed by porous aggregates, and they are crucial for fluid storage and flow. The term also encompasses the internal spaces within the rock, which are particularly relevant in the study of p

Pore Controlling Throats [parameter] — The flow-controlling throats at gas-liquid interfaces where porous aggregates preferentially obstruct flow rather than uniformly filling pore space or grain surfaces.
Time-Lapse 3D X-Ray Imaging [technology] — A method used to demonstrate that halite builds sponge-like structures with 40% internal porosity rather than simply filling pores.
Capillary Forces [parameter] — Capillary forces generated by porous networks that draw brine toward precipitation sites, accelerating growth.
Carbon Storage Efficiency [parameter] — The efficiency of carbon storage that is directly improved by quantitative measurements of salt architecture, reactive surface areas, and pore connectivity.

Agicultural Soil Management [parameter] — The management of agricultural soils that is directly improved by quantitative measurements of salt architecture, reactive surface areas, and pore connectivity.

Cultural Heritage Preservation Strategies [parameter] — Strategies for cultural heritage preservation that are directly improved by quantitative measurements of salt architecture, reactive surface areas, and pore connectivity.
Grain Surfaces [geologicalbody] — The surfaces of rock grains that can adsorb or react with fluids.
Salt Architecture [process] — The structural and functional characteristics of salt deposits, including connectivity, surface area, and pore size distributions.

Reservoir Rocks [geologicalbody] — The rocks in which carbon dioxide (CO2) is stored and through which it can flow.<SEP>The rock formations in the CO2 storage sites where CO2 is stored.<SEP>The rock units where CO2 is stored, with a storage capacity not to exceed 3%.
In-Situ Brine Evaporation [process] — The process by which brine evaporates in-situ when carbon dioxide (CO2) is undersaturated with water.

High-Salinity Aquifers [geologicalbody] — Aquifers with high concentrations of dissolved salts that can affect CO2 storage performance.<SEP>Aquifers with high concentrations of dissolved salts, which can impede CO2 storage performance, injectivity, and containment integrity.
Pore Clogging [process] — The process of clogging pores due to salt precipitation, which reduces permeability and increases injection pressure.
Ketzin [geologicalbody] — A GCS reservoir in Germany, with a high salinity of 230,000 ppm TDS.
Illinois Basin-Decatur [geologicalbody] — A GCS reservoir in the USA, with a high salinity of approximately 200,000 ppm TDS.
Aquitrost (Saskatchewan, Canada) [geologicalbody] — A GCS reservoir in Saskatchewan, Canada, with a high salinity of 330,000 ppm TDS.
Greensand (Denmark) [geologicalbody] — A GCS reservoir in Denmark, with a potential high salinity of over 100,000 ppm TDS.

Capillary Pumping [process] — A mechanism during evaporation-crystallization-precipitation processes under atmospheric conditions at open boundaries, identified in prior studies on salt precipitation.

Creeping Behavior [process] — A mechanism during evaporation-crystallization-precipitation processes under atmospheric conditions at open boundaries, identified in prior studies on salt precipitation.

Efflorescence Formation [process] — A mechanism during evaporation-crystallization-precipitation processes under atmospheric conditions at open boundaries, identified in prior studies on salt precipitation.

GCS [process] — Geological Carbon Storage, a technology for carbon sequestration in the near-wellbore region following two-phase viscous displacement under injection conditions.<SEP>The CO2 capture, utilisation and storage process.<SEP>Geological carbon storage, a process of storing CO2 in deep saline aquifers.

Pore Network [geologicalbody] — Three-dimensional pore networks in porous media.<SEP>The network of interconnected void spaces in a porous medium where fluids can flow and solutes can be transported.<SEP>The network of pores within the Ketton limestone.<SEP>A network of pores and throats in the rock formation, which is the subject of analysis in the context of reactive injection and dissolution.<SEP>A network of interconnected p

Pore Connectivity [parameter] — Measurements of pore network connectivity.<SEP>The connectivity of pores in the rock structure.<SEP>The interconnectedness of pores, which affects the efficacy of capillary-induced brine film flow and the distribution of evaporation sites.<SEP>The measured connectivity of the pores within the porous medium.<SEP>The interconnectivity of pores in porous rocks, another key physical property for under
Surface Area Scaling [parameter] — Measurements of scaling in surface area.<SEP>The scaling relationship of surface area in the rock structure.
Density Gradients [parameter] — Measurements of density changes.<SEP>The gradients in density within the rock structure.
Residual Brine Saturation [process] — The process of remaining brine saturation after the initial displacement and evaporation steps.
Self-Enhancing Feedback Mechanism [process] — A process where the nucleation on existing crystals creates a mechanism that enhances the precipitation of salt.

Reactive Transport Models [technology] — Models used for reactive transport in carbon storage, soil management, and heritage preservation.<SEP>Models used in carbon sequestration.<SEP>Models that implement and capture self-enhancing mechanisms in reactive transport, specifically how porous precipitates create positive feedback.

Residual Brine [material] — The remaining brine after the initial displacement and evaporation steps.<SEP>A remnant of the original brine phase that remains after crystallization.<SEP>Remaining brine after oven drying.
Capillary-Driven Flow [process] — The flow driven by capillary forces that enhances wetting-phase connectivity.<SEP>A physical process where flow is driven by capillary forces.

Concentration Gradients [parameter] — The gradients within the aqueous films that drive molecular diffusion.<SEP>The concentration gradients developing from evaporation fronts toward brine reservoirs at the macroscale.<SEP>The difference in the concentration of solutes across different spatial scales.

Gas-Brine Interface [process] — The interface formed by the interaction of gas and brine in the porous medium.<SEP>The boundary between the gas and brine phases in the porous media, where evaporation is most intense.
Discrete Pools [material] — The discrete pools of nearly immobile aqueous phase formed after drainage.<SEP>Discrete pools of varying sizes formed by nearly immobile aqueous phase after drainage.
Viscous Two-Phase Flow [process] — The flow process during CO2 injection where viscous forces dominate.
Residual Brine Distribution [parameter] — The distribution of residual brine after drainage, with greater retention in smaller pores due to higher capillary pressures.

Evaporative Fronts [process] — The transition of water from the liquid phase to the gas phase, forming evaporative fronts during CO2 injection.<SEP>The boundary where water transitions into the gas phase during CO2 injection.
Brine Pools [parameter] — Pools of residual brine after drainage, with greater retention in smaller pores due to higher capillary pressures.
RTM Hypothesis [technology] — A hypothesis related to the prevailing understanding of rock texture modeling (RTM) in 3D porous media.
Pore-Scale Dynamics [process] — Microscale diffusion and transport processes occurring at the pore level during CO2 injection.
Supersaturated Microenvironments [process] — Local concentration gradients leading to the development of supersaturated conditions.
Secondary Porous Media [geologicalbody] — A new network of small pore sizes formed by continuous evaporation and ion transport processes.
Halite Crystal [material] — A crystal form of the mineral halite, which is sodium chloride.
Pore Geometry [geologicalbody] — The structure and arrangement of pores within the porous medium.<SEP>The precise representation of the pore structure in micro-CT images.
Capillary Redistribution [process] — The process of redistributing fluids through capillary action.
Capillary Pressure Gradient [parameter] — The pressure difference created by capillary forces within the porous medium.
Marangoni Convection [process] — Convection driven by surface tension gradients, leading to the redistribution of solutes.
Solute Redistribution [process] — The process of moving solutes through the porous medium.

Supersaturation [process] — A condition where the concentration of dissolved salt in the brine exceeds the solubility limit, promoting crystal growth.<SEP>A condition in which the concentration of a solute in a solvent exceeds its solubility, leading to the formation of solid precipitates.<SEP>Measure of the extent to which a solution contains dissolved solutes beyond its solubility limit, influencing precipitation sequences

Glass Beads [material] — Small particles used in the flow cell to facilitate the formation of crystalline networks through supersaturation.<SEP>Hydrophilic surfaces that stabilize thin brine films and enhance solute transport.<SEP>Glass beads with a diameter of 2 mm used in the experimental setup.<SEP>Packed with 2 mm (±50 μm) diameter glass beads positioned vertically.<SEP>A material phase identified in the phase segment

Micro-CT [technology] — A non-destructive imaging technique used to visualize the internal structures of solid materials, particularly useful in the study of porous media.<SEP>A type of X-ray computed tomography used for detailed microstructural analysis.<SEP>A micro-computed tomography technique used for scanning rock samples at different resolutions.
Gas-liquid Interface [geologicalbody] — The boundary between the gas and liquid phases in a porous medium, where solute deposition and mineral formation can occur.
Meniscus [geologicalbody] — The curved surface of a liquid in a narrow tube or porous medium, which can influence the behavior of ions and the formation of minerals.

Capillary Effects [process] — The phenomenon by which liquids rise or fall in narrow tubes due to intermolecular forces, which play a role in the stabilization of thin, supersaturated films in porous media.
Thermodynamic Equilibrium [process] — A state in which a system is in a state of balance, where the properties do not change over time, relevant to the coexistence of brine and salt.
Pore Throats [geologicalbody] — Narrow passages within rock formations that restrict fluid flow.<SEP>The narrow passages connecting larger pores in the rock.
Porous Structures [process] — Structures with elevated liquid saturation created by retained internal brine.
Internal Brine [material] — Retained brine that sustains continued growth of porous structures.
Oven Drying [process] — A process of drying samples in an oven.
Glass Bead [material] — A spherical object used in the experiment.<SEP>Surface on which halite nucleates and extends into adjacent pore spaces.
Brine-Salt Interactions [process] — The interaction between brine and salt around a glass bead.
Phase Volumes [process] — Quantified volumes of phases (brine, salt, and voids) in the flow cell.
Voids [material] — Empty spaces in the porous media that increase as water saturation approaches zero.
Phase Volume Distributions [parameter] — Measurable quantities of the volume occupied by different phases in the porous media.
Kernel Density Estimates (KDE) [technology] — Methods used to reveal phase volume distributions and spatial variability.
Salt Volume [parameter] — Measurable quantities of the volume occupied by salt in the porous media.

Halite's hygroscopicity further enhances moisture retention, maintaining local supersaturation.

Rock Physics [technology] — The process of modeling the physical properties of rocks, especially for seismic velocity predictions.

Trajectory Length [parameter] — A measurable quantity related to the length of trajectories in the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo algorithm.<SEP>A parameter in Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) that defines the length of the trajectory of particles.

No-U-Turn Sampler [technology] — A method for automatic selection of trajectory lengths in Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) sampling.

Variational Inference (VI) [technology] — A method for approximating the posterior distribution with a parameterized distribution family.

Multi-Chain Sampling [technology] — A method to sample from the posterior distribution using multiple chains to explore different modes.

Multi-objective Optimization [process] — Optimization process to find the Pareto front of solutions that maximize all companies’ NPVs under pressure constraints.
Operational Limits [parameter] — Constraints on the decisions made by companies.

Pareto Front [parameter] — The set of solutions in the objective space that are not dominated by any other solution.<SEP>A set of non-dominated solutions representing trade-offs between objectives in CMOO problems<SEP>A concept in multi-operator CCS settings, used to enumerate all possible solutions under centralized optimization but does not specify outcomes under decentralized decision making.<SEP>The set of non-dominated

Pareto Optimal Solutions [parameter] — Solutions in the objective space that form the Pareto front, where improving one objective necessarily degrades the other.<SEP>Points on the Pareto front where no objective can be improved without degrading another
CMOO [process] — Multi-objective optimization process for decision-making<SEP>Constrained multi-objective optimization using NSGA-II.

NSGA-II [technology] — Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II, a method for solving CMOO problems<SEP>A constrained multi-objective optimization algorithm used to produce Pareto fronts.<SEP>A method used in the study for obtaining the Pareto front.<SEP>A multi-objective optimization algorithm.
PyMOO [technology] — A framework used for implementing NSGA-II for CMOO problems
Pareto Front Post-Optimization [parameter] — The process of selecting a single implementable operating strategy from the Pareto front
Knee Point [parameter] — A point on the Pareto front often chosen as the preferred solution in post-optimization
Pareto Optimal Set [parameter] — The set of solutions that are not dominated by any other solution in the solution space
Centralized Decision Maker [risk] — A single decision maker with complete knowledge of basin-scale reservoir conditions and operational strategies of all stakeholders
Multi-Operator CCS [risk] — CCS operations involving multiple independent operators with limited information and potentially competing interests

Constrained Markov Game [technology] — A reformulated optimization problem using multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to address multi-stakeholder geological carbon storage (GCS), where each operator acts as an autonomous agent with safety constraints.<SEP>A game formulation that restricts agents to a feasible action space to ensure compliance with operational and regulatory safety requirements.

Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) [technology] — A method used in the constrained Markov game to learn an optimal policy for each stakeholder operating in the shared reservoir environment.<SEP>A framework for reinforcement learning involving multiple agents with shared or overlapping objectives.
Shared Reservoir Environment [geologicalbody] — The common environment in which all operators interact, subject to safety constraints and pursuing individual economic goals.

Point-Selection Approaches [technology] — Methods used in optimization problems to select a single implementable operating strategy, which may not align with what is operationally feasible given contractual, regulatory, or organizational constraints.
Decentralized Decision Making [risk] — The decision-making process where stakeholders make decisions independently, which can differ from centralized optimization outcomes.
Conventional CMOO [technology] — A common optimization approach for modeling real multioperator CCS decision-making environments, which may not fully represent the practical limitations.
Optimization Problem [process] — The problem of finding the best strategy for all operators in the shared reservoir environment, reformulated as a constrained Markov game.

Deep Reinforcement Learning [technology] — A branch of machine learning designed for sequential decision-making problems where labeled training data are unavailable, and agents must learn optimal behaviors through repeated interactions with the environment.
Carbon Storage [process] — The process of storing carbon dioxide in geological formations to mitigate climate change.
DAS/DTS [technology] — Distributed Acoustic Sensing and Distributed Temperature Sensing technologies used to monitor subsurface conditions and detect anomalies.

Policy [technology] — The strategy or mapping from observations to actions in a Markov Decision Process, learned through the reinforcement learning process.<SEP>A strategy or approach used in the carbon storage demonstration to illustrate the performance of the approach.

Markov Game Setting [process] — A framework with n agents where each agent has an action space, a reward function, and a policy, and the environment transitions according to the joint actions of all agents.
Schematic Diagram [material] — A visual representation of the frameworks for single- and multi-agent RL, including Markov decision process and Markov game.
State-Conditioned Policy [process] — A policy that depends on the state of the environment and is used to maximize the long-term return of each agent.
State-Value Function [process] — A function that assigns a value to each state, which represents the expected return starting from that state and following a particular policy.
Action-Value Function [process] — A function that assigns a value to each action, which represents the expected return starting from a particular state and following a particular action.
Injection Control [process] — The process of managing the injection of CO2 into the subsurface environment at discrete management intervals.
Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning [technology] — A safe reinforcement learning framework that extends MARL by integrating safety constraints into the decision-making process.
Plume Saturation [parameter] — A measurable quantity such as plume saturation that is observed and used in the optimization process.
Alphabetical Pressure Threshold [parameter] — The allowable threshold pressure (pgrid ≤αpfrac) that pore pressure at well locations or each grid cell must not exceed.
Lagrangian Objective [process] — A process used to train the actor network in the reinforcement learning framework.
Safety [risk] — A failure mode or hazard related to the pressure limits in the subsurface environment.
Markov Game/Safe-MARL Framework [technology] — A constrained Markov game/safe-MARL framework used for geological CO2 storage, not restricted to pressure.
Geological CO2 Storage (GCS) [process] — The process of storing CO2 in geological formations, where rewards and penalties must balance economic returns and regulatory compliance.
Reward Structure [technology] — A classification of reward structures in multi-agent reinforcement learning, including fully competitive, fully cooperative, or mixed competitive–cooperative.

Threshold [parameter] — A prescribed pressure level that the pore pressure in the injection-well grid block should not exceed.<SEP>The threshold value (ε) used to determine the contribution to δs.<SEP>A value used to determine the level of error acceptable for the surrogate models.
Project Area [geologicalbody] — The spatial extent of the project area within which the grid blocks are located.
Lagrangian Multipliers [technology] — Variables used to enforce safety constraints during the training process.
Decentralized Control [technology] — A control mechanism where each operator controls its own wells based on local observations.

Permeability Distribution [parameter] — The permeability distribution for the basin, shown in Figure 6.<SEP>The heterogeneous permeability of the reservoir, assumed to follow a statistical distribution p(κ) for simulation.<SEP>A distribution used to generate samples for capturing statistics on fracture occurrence.<SEP>A measurable quantity used to capture statistics on the fracture occurrence frequency.

Company C [other] — A company operating in the synthetic basin area.<SEP>A company involved in the study, which gains substantial benefits from coalition formation with NPV gains of $1255 million.<SEP>An organization involved in the CCUS process.<SEP>A company involved in the study, alongside Company A and Company B.<SEP>A company involved in the study.

Process [UNKNOWN] — GCS is a process that must balance economic returns and regulatory compliance through rewards and penalties.

Flat Three-Dimensional Reservoir Model [geologicalbody] — A simplified model of a clastic shelf depositional environment used to validate the workflow.
True-3D Reservoir Model [geologicalbody] — A detailed model used to generate intelligent treatments for bridging quantities between true-3D and single-layer reservoir models.

Single-Layer Reservoir Model [geologicalbody] — A simplified model used in the workflow to forecast reservoir performance.<SEP>A reservoir model that simplifies the reservoir into a single layer for easier simulation.

Ensemble Smoother Multiple Data Assimilation (ES-MDA) Framework [technology] — A framework used to update geologic properties and predict reservoir performance with quantified uncertainty from pressure history and CO2 plumes interpreted through seismic inversion.

Data Assimilation [process] — The process of computing probability density function of a model solution conditioned on measured observations.<SEP>The process of integrating monitoring data into subsequent forecasts to improve accuracy and provide quantified uncertainties.<SEP>The methods and models used to integrate observed data into a model to improve its accuracy.
Inverse Problems [process] — The process of solving for model parameters given the observed data.
Reservoir Management [process] — The process of managing reservoirs to optimize performance and ensure safety.

Geologic Carbon Storage (GCS) [process] — The process of storing carbon dioxide in geological formations to mitigate climate change.<SEP>A method of storing carbon dioxide in geological formations, which can handle multimodal time-lapse data and control CO2 injectivity to mitigate reservoir fracturing risks.
Geological Fluid Flow [process] — The movement of fluids within geological formations.

Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF) [technology] — A fast approximate method for high-dimensional inversion problems used in subsurface reservoir models.<SEP>A method for high-dimensional inversion problems, where data is assimilated sequentially in time.<SEP>A filter used for model parameterization based on truncated singular value decomposition (SVD).

Ensemble Smoother (ES) [technology] — A fast approximate method for high-dimensional inversion problems used in subsurface reservoir models.<SEP>A method for high-dimensional inversion problems, where data is combined into one assimilation step.
Parameter Space [parameter] — The space of possible values for parameters in a model, particularly in subsurface reservoir models.<SEP>The range of values for parameters in the reservoir model.

Ensemble Kalman Filter [technology] — A method for high-dimensional inversion problems, where data is assimilated sequentially in time.<SEP>A method used in history matching for carbon storage operations.<SEP>A popular approach among ensemble-based methods for updating belief distributions.<SEP>A popular ensemble-based approach for sequential data simulation in the estimation of state uncertainties.

Ensemble Smoother [technology] — A method for high-dimensional inversion problems, where data is combined into one assimilation step.<SEP>A method that assimilates all data simultaneously in a single update, reducing the need for simulation restarts.

Area of Review (AOR) [parameter] — The region surrounding the storage project where underground sources of drinking water may be endangered by injection activity.

CNNs [technology] — CNNs (Convolutional Neural Networks) are a type of deep learning model used for image and signal processing, particularly in the context of surrogate modeling for subsurface flow.

Convolutional Encoder-Decoder Network [technology] — A convolutional encoder-decoder network is a deep learning model used to estimate pressure and velocity fields in single-phase steady-state flow under geologic uncertainties.

Conditional Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network [technology] — A conditional convolutional generative adversarial network is a deep learning model used to predict CO2 plume migration from a single injection well in the context of multiphase dynamic flow.

Residual U-Net (R-U-Net) [technology] — A residual U-Net is a deep learning model used for predicting CO2 plume migration in single-well injection scenarios under different permeability fields, injection durations, injection rates, and injection locations.

Recurrent R-U-Net [technology] — A recurrent R-U-Net is a deep learning model used to predict two-dimensional and three-dimensional dynamic pressure and saturation maps for oil production data assimilation.

Data Assimilation Problem [process] — A problem addressed in Section 5 where surrogate models are applied to evaluate the model performance.<SEP>A problem that surrogate models were applied to in the workflow.
Cap Rock [geologicalbody] — The top two layers of the discretized reservoir model, assumed to be shale.<SEP>The rock unit that acts as a seal to prevent the upward migration of CO2.
Clastic Shelf Depositional Environment [geologicalbody] — The depositional environment of the reservoir model.
Porosity and Permeability Distributions [parameter] — Based on the median quantities for the clastic shelf depositional environment.

Carter-Tracy Aquifer Model [technology] — Aquifer model (Carter and Tracy, 1960)

ES-MDA [technology] — An efficient ensemble-based method used for updating model parameters based on perturbed observation data.<SEP>A specific ensemble-based framework used in the workflow.<SEP>A method used to sample from the posterior of porosity given both d2 and φcond.

Reservoir Models [technology] — Models representing the geological structure of the reservoir.<SEP>Models used to simulate the behavior of the storage formation.<SEP>Calibrated reservoir models used to reduce uncertainties in reservoir forecasts.
Initial Ensemble Design [parameter] — The design of the initial ensemble which is crucial for ensemble-based methods.

Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) [technology] — A type of derivative-free method used for history matching that involves fewer underlying assumptions but may require large numbers of function evaluations.<SEP>A hierarchical statistical method used in the history matching procedure.
Uncertainty Reduction [parameter] — A measurable quantity indicating the reduction in uncertainties of key geomodel parameters.

4D Seismic [material] — A type of seismic data collected over time to monitor changes in subsurface conditions.

Ensemble Smoother with Multiple Data Assimilation [technology] — A method used in history matching for carbon storage operations.<SEP>A commonly used ensemble-based inference method for estimating state uncertainties, reducing computational cost of belief updates.
Gradient-Based Methods [technology] — A category of history matching algorithms that require gradient information.
Derivative-Free Methods [technology] — A category of history matching algorithms that do not require gradient information.
Multivariate Adaptive Regression Spline (MARS) [technology] — A surrogate model used in CO2 storage modeling and data assimilation.
Bagging MARS (BMARS) [technology] — A surrogate model used for calibration of a CO2 reservoir model.
Gaussian-Process-Based Surrogate Model [technology] — A surrogate model applied to history match a coalbed methane reservoir.
Differentiable Neural Network (DNN) [technology] — A surrogate model used to obtain gradient information for history matching.
Reduced-Order Model (ROM) [technology] — A model used to accelerate history matching of fractured simulation models.

Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) [technology] — A type of neural network used in the development of deep learning models for subsurface flow.<SEP>A type of artificial neural network used for image recognition and upscaling of permeability information.
Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) [technology] — A type of neural network used in the development of deep learning models for subsurface flow.
Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) [technology] — A type of neural network architecture considered for subsurface flow modeling.
Graph Neural Networks (GNN) [technology] — A type of neural network architecture considered for subsurface flow modeling.
Fourier Neural Operators (FNO) [technology] — A type of neural network architecture considered for subsurface flow modeling.
Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) Network [technology] — A type of recurrent neural network used for constructing surrogate models for subsurface flow problems.

Hierarchical Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) Method [technology] — A method used for estimating posterior scenario parameters in CO2 storage problems.<SEP>A hierarchical MCMC method used for sampling geomodels and evaluating the likelihood based on data mismatch.
Theory-Guided CNN (TgCNN) [technology] — A type of CNN incorporating domain knowledge for two-phase subsurface flow problems.
Iterative Ensemble Smoother [technology] — A method used for history matching combined with TgCNN surrogates.
Bayesian MCMC [technology] — A method used for combining with LSTM-based surrogate models for history matching.<SEP>A method used in combination with LSTM-based surrogate models for history matching.
Time-Lapse (4D) Seismic Data [material] — Seismic data used for monitoring changes over time in oil/gas production and geological CO2 storage settings.
LSTM-Based Surrogate Model [technology] — A surrogate model used to predict the oil recovery factor based on LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) technology.
Reservoir Monitoring [process] — The process of using 4D seismic data to monitor time-varying pressure and saturation in reservoirs.
Petro-Elastic Modeling [technology] — A computationally expensive forward seismic modeling method used in reservoir simulation.
Forward Seismic Modeling [technology] — The process of modeling seismic data, often involving petro-elastic modeling, to understand subsurface flow and reservoir dynamics.
ESMDA [technology] — A method used in the history matching of Brazilian deep water heavy-oil reservoirs, combining production data and 4D seismic data.

3D U-Net [technology] — A deep learning model used in this study to process highly resolved geomodel data.<SEP>A deep learning model architecture used for predicting interpreted 4D seismic saturation fields.

1D U-Net [technology] — A deep learning model used in this study to predict monitoring well data with multiple channels corresponding to time steps.<SEP>A deep learning model architecture used for predicting monitoring well data.<SEP>A 1D U-Net used for predicting monitoring well data.
MCMC Method [technology] — A hierarchical Markov Chain Monte Carlo method used in this study for history matching.

Seismic Surrogate Model [technology] — A deep learning model used in this study to process seismic data.<SEP>A model used to generate interpreted seismic saturation fields.<SEP>A model used as a surrogate for the true seismic model, faster and more manageable.
Seismic Saturation [process] — The CO2 saturation value estimated by seismic data.<SEP>A process for observing the saturation of reservoirs using seismic techniques.
Seismic Saturation (Seismic Data) [parameter] — The CO2 saturation value estimated by seismic data.
Seismic Saturation (Seismic Data Only) [parameter] — The presence or absence of CO2 indicated by seismic data.
Hierarchical MCMC Method [technology] — A hierarchical Markov Chain Monte Carlo method used for history matching.<SEP>Method used for history matching and data assimilation.
Geomodels [geologicalbody] — Geological models used in the study, including their uncertain metaparameters and detailed heterogeneous realizations.
Full Domain [geologicalbody] — The full model with dimensions 109 km × 109 km × 70 m, discretized into 148 × 148 × 35 cells (total of 766,640 cells).

Surrounding Region [geologicalbody] — A large region surrounding the storage aquifer, used for pressure dissipation, with dimensions 109 km × 109 km × 70 m, discretized into 148 × 148 × 35 cells (total of 766,640 cells).
No-Flow Boundary Conditions [parameter] — Boundary conditions applied on the outer boundaries of the surrounding region and at the top and bottom of the model.

High-Resolution Central Storage Aquifer Domain [geologicalbody] — A high-resolution domain centered on the storage aquifer with dimensions 128 × 128 × 35 cells (total of 573,440 cells), each cell being 7 m × 7 m × 2 m.
Large Cells [geologicalbody] — Cells used in the surrounding region with dimensions 70 m × 70 m × 70 m, which are not a significant issue since very little CO2 reaches this portion of the model.
Vertical Injection Well [wellborecomponent] — A fully penetrating vertical well placed near the center of the storage aquifer, at i = 65, j = 65, as shown in Figure 1(b).
Log-Permeability Field [parameter] — A field representing the log of permeability, characterized by mean (µlog k) and standard deviation (σlog k).
Vertical Permeability [parameter] — The vertical permeability of the storage aquifer, denoted by kv.<SEP>The vertical permeability, denoted as kv.
Horizontal Permeability [parameter] — The horizontal permeability of the storage aquifer, denoted by kh.<SEP>The horizontal permeability, denoted as kh.
Injector Well [wellborecomponent] — A well used for injecting CO2 into the storage aquifer.
Log-permeability Field [parameter] — A field representing the log of permeability, with mean and standard deviation.
Log-permeability [parameter] — The log-permeability field in the storage aquifer, represented as log ks.
MCMC Procedure [technology] — A procedure applied to reduce uncertainty ranges of metaparameters.
SVD [process] — Singular value decomposition applied to the matrix containing centered realizations generated using SGeMS.<SEP>A method used for obtaining the basis matrix in the PCA representation.
Stochastic Vector [parameter] — A vector with each component sampled from N(0, 1) used in the PCA-based realization.

KZ [parameter] — A parameter used to represent the vertical permeability in the full storage aquifer geomodel, calculated as a function of horizontal permeability.
Cutoffs [parameter] — A process involving the application of limits to the PCA-generated permeability and porosity values to avoid extreme (nonphysical) values.
Gas (Supercritical CO2) [material] — A chemical species, specifically in a state of being a supercritical fluid, which is the focus of the 4D seismic monitoring.

Plume Location [parameter] — A parameter representing the presence of gas above a certain threshold saturation, used in the interpreted estimates of 4D seismic data.<SEP>Presence of gas above some threshold saturation, interpreted at the resolution of 4D seismic data.<SEP>The area where CO2 is predicted to spread in the subsurface.<SEP>A measurable quantity related to the location of the CO2 plume.<SEP>The location of the CO2

Interpreted Seismic Data [parameter] — Seismic data generated from flow simulation results, with a resolution of 21 m × 21 m × 10 m, corresponding to a 3 × 3 × 5 filtering of fine-scale saturation fields.
Fine-Scale Saturation Fields [parameter] — Original CO2 saturation fields on a grid of dimensions 128 × 128 × 35, with cells of size 7 m × 7 m × 2 m.

Filtered Saturation Fields [parameter] — Saturation fields after applying a two-step filtering process, with a resolution of 21 m × 21 m × 10 m.<SEP>Fine-scale saturation fields after being filtered through a two-step process.
Seismic Data Interpretation [technology] — The process of interpreting seismic data to provide an estimate of CO2 saturation using full-waveform inversion or deep learning models.
Plume Location Identification [risk] — The identification of the presence or absence of the CO2 plume based on seismic data.

Binary Image [material] — A representation of plume location with values of 1 where the plume is present and 0 otherwise.<SEP>A representation of plume location with a value of 1 where the plume is present and 0 otherwise.
Sg [parameter] — A measurable quantity representing seismic saturation.
Threshold Value [parameter] — The detection limit or threshold value for plume presence, set to 0.05 in this work.
Interpreted Seismic Saturation Data [material] — Generated interpreted seismic saturation data from a high-fidelity geomodel.

Interpreted Plume Location Data [parameter] — Generated binary plume location data from a high-fidelity geomodel.<SEP>Data interpreted from the plume location used in the analysis.<SEP>Data indicating the location of CO2 plume based on interpreted 4D seismic data.

Deep Learning Surrogate Models [technology] — Models used to reduce the computational burden of generating flow simulation results for history matching.

MCMC-based History Matching [process] — A procedure that requires a large number of flow simulation results for evaluation of the likelihood function, but is inefficient for high-fidelity simulations.
Monitoring-well Data [material] — Data collected at high vertical resolution but at one (or potentially a few) spatial locations, used for monitoring purposes.
Interpreted Seismic Prediction [process] — A process for generating interpreted seismic data from high-fidelity simulation results.

Interpreted Saturation Field [parameter] — A field that estimates either seismic-scale Sg or plume location.

U-Net Architecture [technology] — A network architecture used for the interpreted seismic surrogate model.
Interpreted Seismic Surrogate Model [technology] — A model used for approximating the relationship between geomodel properties and interpreted seismic saturation fields.
Geos [technology] — A software tool used for flow simulation in the context of the seismic surrogate model.

It outputs a series of 1D vectors representing predicted saturation values for all nz cells at the monitoring location at a particular time.<SEP>A 1D U-Net model used for predicting monitoring well data.

Metropolis–Hastings [technology] — A method used for generating a sequence of random samples from a probability distribution, especially in the context of Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods.
MCMC [technology] — A class of algorithms for sampling from a probability distribution based on constructing a Markov chain that has the desired distribution as its equilibrium distribution.

Likelihood [parameter] — A measure of the probability of observing the data given a particular set of parameters.<SEP>The probability of observing the data given the model parameters, which is used to evaluate the fit of the model to the data.
