Geophysics [process] — A field of study concerned with the application of physical methods to the investigation of the Earth, integrated with reservoir engineering for monitoring CO2 storage projects.
Reservoir Engineering [process] — A field of study concerned with the management of reservoirs to recover oil, gas, or water, integrated with geophysics for monitoring CO2 storage projects.

Cap Rock Fracturing [risk] — A failure mode where the cap rock integrity is compromised during CO2 storage operations, leading to potential environmental hazards.<SEP>A risk mode where caprock integrity is compromised during CO2 storage operations.
Simulation-Based Inference [technology] — A method of estimating the posterior density of a model through simulations, employed in the Digital Twin for geologic carbon storage.

Sequential Bayesian Inference [technology] — A statistical method used to update the probability of a hypothesis as more evidence becomes available, employed in the Digital Twin for geologic carbon storage.
Monitoring Wells [wellborecomponent] — Wells used for collecting data during CO2 storage operations.<SEP>Wells used to monitor the CO2 saturation.
GenAI [technology] — Generative Artificial Intelligence methodologies used in Digital Twins.
Fracture Probability [risk] — The probability that a fracture will occur in the reservoir.<SEP>A measurable quantity representing the likelihood of fracturing occurring during CO2 injection.

Bernoulli Distribution [process] — A statistical distribution used to model binary events, such as fracture/no-fracture occurrences.<SEP>A probability distribution of a binary random variable, which can take only two values, 0 or 1.
Confidence Interval [parameter] — A measurable quantity indicating the range within which the true value of a parameter is expected to lie with a certain level of confidence.
Cumulative Density Function (CDF) [process] — A mathematical function used to calculate the probability that a random variable takes a value less than or equal to a given value.
Well Data [process] — Data collected from wells to inform the Digital Twin's state samples.

Conditional Normalizing Flow [technology] — A method used in the series of numerical experiments to infer flow patterns for regular and irregular flow from well and seismic data.<SEP>A machine learning model used to generate samples from the posterior distribution of CO2 saturation given seismic and well data.
Regular Flow [process] — A predictable flow pattern of CO2 in the subsurface.<SEP>The flow scenario where reservoir properties are kept constant, resulting in regular CO2 plumes.

Irregular Flow [process] — An unpredictable flow pattern of CO2 in the subsurface, often caused by leakage.<SEP>The flow scenario where permeability changes at the reservoir’s seal, leading to an instantaneous permeability increase and CO2 plume leakage.
Fluid Flow Simulations [process] — Simulations used to model the movement of fluids in the reservoir.
Conditioned Normalizing Flows [technology] — A method used to produce high-fidelity estimates for CO2 plumes with or without leakage.
Seismic Reflection Data [material] — Data obtained from seismic imaging to reflect the subsurface structure.

Conditional Normalizing Flows [technology] — A method used to approximate posteriors of seismic imaging and handle non-uniqueness in nonlinear phenomena.<SEP>A method used to capture subtle pattern changes during inference in a setting where training pairs consist of realizations for CO2 saturation and associated time-lapse data.
Multi-Modal Time-Lapse Monitoring Data [parameter] — Observed data used to improve inferences of CO2-flow patterns and their uncertainty.
CO2 Saturation Image [parameter] — A measurable quantity related to the concentration of CO2 in the saturation images.
Time-Lapse Observables [parameter] — Measurable quantities, specifically time-lapse observations used to condition the posterior distribution.
Devito [technology] — Devito, a just-in-time compiler, is used for seismic data modeling and imaging.
Model-Parallel Fourier Neural Operators [technology] — The computational surrogate method used to enhance the adaptability of fluid flow simulations to large-scale four-dimensional scenarios.

Seismic Baseline Survey [process] — The seismic survey representing the initial stage before CO2 is injected, serving as the baseline for time-lapse seismic imaging.<SEP>A seismic survey conducted before CO2 injection to establish a baseline for subsequent monitoring.

Seismic Monitor Survey [process] — The seismic survey corresponding to the time of 8 years after CO2 injection, used to observe changes in the Earth’s acoustic properties.<SEP>A seismic survey conducted 8 years after CO2 injection to monitor changes in the subsurface.
Reverse Time Migration (RTM) [technology] — A technique used to create time-lapse seismic images of the subsurface by reversing the time of seismic data.
Time-Lapse Seismic Images [material] — Seismic images created to monitor changes in the subsurface over time due to CO2 injection.
Training Pairs [parameter] — Data sets used for training the network, consisting of pairs of input and output data.

Seismic Observations [technology] — Seismic data collected to image the subsurface.<SEP>A measurable quantity derived from seismic imaging, used for imaging observations in the reservoir.<SEP>Seismic surveys and spatial filtering techniques used to observe the saturation of CO2 plumes before drilling each injector.<SEP>The process of gathering information about the saturation of the reservoir using seismic techniques.
Pressure Well [material] — Data from pressure measurements taken in the wellbore during the study.<SEP>A component of a wellbore used to measure the pressure in the reservoir.
Saturation Well Data [material] — Data from wellbore measurements of CO2 saturation.<SEP>A measurable quantity derived from wellbore data, used to determine the saturation of the reservoir.
No-Leakage Case [parameter] — A scenario where CO2 injection does not result in any leakage.
Leakage Case [parameter] — A scenario where CO2 injection results in leakage.
Seismic Plume [geologicalbody] — A geological body representing the spread of CO2 in the reservoir.
Time-Lapse Seismic Observations [process] — Seismic observations taken over time to monitor changes in the reservoir.
Numerical Experiments [technology] — Carefully designed experiments to demonstrate the capability of conditional normalizing flows in capturing subtle pattern changes.
Seismic Images [material] — Images obtained from seismic observations used in the research.
Well Measurements [material] — Data obtained from wellbore components used in the research.

Training Dataset [technology] — The 3D Compass Velocity Model is used to create the training dataset for the conditional normalizing flows.<SEP>A dataset composed of extracted raw subvolumes and their corresponding permeability data.

Carbon Storage Operations [process] — Operations related to storing carbon dioxide in geological formations.<SEP>The operational processes involved in capturing and storing carbon dioxide in a geological formation.<SEP>The process of storing carbon dioxide in geological formations to mitigate climate change.

Belief State Planning [technology] — A method for solving the POMDP to optimize injector and monitoring well locations.<SEP>A method for planning the operations of carbon storage initiatives by considering the current state of the system.
POMDP Decision-Making Process [process] — The process of making decisions using the POMDP model.<SEP>A process used to handle the complex dynamics of the multi-phase flow.
Multi-Phase Flow [process] — The flow of multiple phases of fluid in porous media.<SEP>The process of flow in porous media involving multiple phases, such as CO2 and brine.
Neural Network Surrogate Model [technology] — A surrogate model using a neural network for the POMDP decision-making process.
Decarbonizing of the Global Energy System [risk] — A process aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions from the global energy system.
Depleted Oil and Gas Reservoir [geologicalbody] — A type of geological formation used in CO2 storage projects.

Coal Seam [geologicalbody] — A type of geological formation used in CO2 storage projects.<SEP>A type of CO₂ storage option for enhanced coalbed methane.<SEP>A coal seam is a layer of coal deposits in the earth.<SEP>A type of geological body where coal is stored.
Power Plants [geologicalbody] — Industrial facilities that emit CO2 and are sources for CO2 capture in CCUS projects.<SEP>Sites where carbon capture could be implemented.
Industrial Facilities [wellborecomponent] — Industrial sources that emit CO2 and are sources for CO2 capture in CCUS projects.
Mineral Precipitations [process] — The process where minerals form in solution, which can occur during CO2 storage projects.
Subsurface Uncertainty [parameter] — The level of uncertainty associated with subsurface conditions in CO2 storage projects.
Induced Earthquakes [risk] — Seismic events caused by CO2 injection into geological formations, posing safety concerns in CCUS projects.
Fractured Cap Rock [risk] — The condition where the cap rock is fractured, leading to potential CO2 leakage in CCUS projects.
Reactivation of Faults [risk] — The condition where faults are reactivated, leading to potential CO2 leakage in CCUS projects.
Injector Location [parameter] — The specific location in the geological formation where CO2 is injected.

POMDP [technology] — The framework for making sequential decisions under uncertainties in carbon storage operations.<SEP>Partially Observable Markov Decision Process<SEP>A technology used in decision-making processes, particularly for sequential decisions in complex environments.
Seismic Signals [parameter] — The seismic signals used for active and passive monitoring of carbon storage operations.

3D Saline Aquifer Reservoir [geologicalbody] — A 3D model of a saline aquifer reservoir used to demonstrate carbon capture operations.<SEP>A 3D geological model of a saline aquifer used in carbon capture operations.
Pomdp [technology] — A decision-making framework used to solve the carbon storage problem by formulating it as a partially observable Markov decision process.
Approximate Belief State Planning [technology] — A method used to solve the carbon storage problem formulated as a POMDP.
3D Geological Porosity Map [parameter] — A 3D map used to model the geological porosity of the 3D saline aquifer reservoir.
CO2 Injector [wellborecomponent] — A component used to inject CO2 into the 3D saline aquifer reservoir.

Free CO2 [material] — CO2 that remains in the aquifer but is not physically bounded and is therefore movable.<SEP>CO2 that remains in the aquifer but is not physically bounded and is, therefore, movable.

Trapped CO2 [parameter] — CO2 that is already in equilibrium and chemically or physically trapped within the aquifer.<SEP>The amount of CO2 that remains in the geological formation after the injection and post-injection period.

3D Porosity Map [parameter] — A three-dimensional representation of the porosity field within the aquifer.<SEP>A three-dimensional map indicating the porosity at various locations within the storage area.
Well Configurations [parameter] — The arrangement of wells in the aquifer.
Trapped CO2 Mass [parameter] — The total mass of trapped CO2.<SEP>The mass of CO2 that is trapped in the geological formation.
Free CO2 Mass [parameter] — The total mass of free CO2.<SEP>The mass of CO2 that is free to move in the geological formation.
CO2 Injectors [wellborecomponent] — Wells used to inject CO2 into the aquifer.
Multi-Phase Flow Simulator [technology] — A computational model that simulates the migration and mass of CO2.
Reward Function [process] — A function that penalizes the total amount of CO2 escaping from the aquifer and positively rewards the total trapped CO2 mass.
Cnn [technology] — A type of neural network used for predicting temporal evolution of trapped, free, and exited CO2.
Fno [technology] — A Fourier Neural Operator used for predicting 4D (3D space-time) CO2 gas saturation distribution.<SEP>A neural network architecture used for predicting CO2 storage and migration.
Well Location [geologicalbody] — The position of an injection well in the geological formation.<SEP>The specific location within an aquifer where direct measurements of porosity are taken.
CO2 Mass [parameter] — The mass of CO2 in the geological formation.<SEP>The mass of CO2 trapped, free, and exited over time.<SEP>The mass of CO2 in the simulation, trained using CNN models.
Mobile CO2 Mass [parameter] — The mass of CO2 that is mobile and can be transported in the geological formation.

Cnn Model [technology] — A Convolutional Neural Network model used to map dynamic 3D gas saturation at each time step into time series predictions of CO2 mass.<SEP>A machine learning model trained using the prepared dataset.
Trapped Co2 Mass [parameter] — One of the three channels in the CNN model used to represent trapped CO2 mass.
Free Co2 Mass [parameter] — One of the three channels in the CNN model used to represent free CO2 mass.
Mobile Co2 Mass [parameter] — One of the three channels in the CNN model used to represent mobile CO2 mass.

Random Policy [technology] — A baseline approach where injectors are selected randomly.<SEP>A policy generated randomly for comparison with the expert and proposed approaches in carbon capture and storage operations.

Expert Policy [technology] — A baseline approach where experts use their knowledge of the aquifer’s geological characteristics and subsurface flow processes to determine injector locations.<SEP>A pre-existing and widely recognized carbon capture and storage policy.
Belief State Planning Policies [technology] — A set of baseline approaches that include random and expert policies, as well as the proposed method.
Injector 1 [geologicalbody] — An injector used for CO2 injection.<SEP>A well used for injecting CO2.
Injector 2 [geologicalbody] — An injector used for CO2 injection.<SEP>A well used for injecting CO2.
Injector 3 [geologicalbody] — An injector used for CO2 injection.<SEP>A well used for injecting CO2.
3D Co2 Saturation Map [parameter] — A 3D map of CO2 saturation used to illustrate the action taken in the simulation.
3D CO2 Saturation Map [process] — A three-dimensional map showing the distribution of CO2 saturation.

3D Saline Aquifer [geologicalbody] — A three-dimensional structure of a saline aquifer used for carbon storage.<SEP>A 3D geological body with an extension of eighty grid blocks in the x- and y-direction and eight blocks in the z-direction.
POMDP Specification [technology] — A specification for a partially observable Markov decision process used for individual components in the carbon storage approach.
Leaked CO2 [parameter] — The amount of CO2 that escapes from the geological formation after the injection and post-injection period.
Trained Surrogate Model [technology] — A surrogate model that has been trained to better represent the complex decision environment in carbon capture and storage operations.
Expected Discounted Return [parameter] — A metric that combines the discounted future returns of a policy, indicating the overall effectiveness and safety of the policy.

Standard Error of Discounted Return [parameter] — A metric that measures the variability of the discounted future returns of a policy, indicating the robustness of the performance around the expected discounted return.
High-Fidelity Surrogate Model [technology] — A surrogate model trained with high fidelity levels for predicting CO2 mass and MRST outputs.
Low-Fidelity Surrogate Model [technology] — A surrogate model trained with low fidelity levels for predicting CO2 mass and MRST outputs.
JS-Divergence [parameter] — Jensen-Shannon Divergences between the density curves of high and low fidelity surrogate model predictions.
Injectors [geologicalbody] — Structural features used for CO2 injection, part of the decision-making process in the study.<SEP>Wells used for the injection of fluids into the 3D saline aquifer.
CO2 Mass Profile [parameter] — A measurable quantity representing the distribution of CO2 in the subsurface at the end of the post-injection period.
POMDP Formulation [technology] — A computational framework used for sequential decision-making under uncertainty, particularly in the context of planning with a monitoring well.
Action Space [parameter] — The set of actions available in the POMDP formulation, which may include the use of a monitoring well.
Observation Space [parameter] — The set of observations available in the POMDP formulation, which changes when the monitoring well is included.
Expected Discounted Reward [parameter] — The anticipated cumulative reward over time in the context of decision-making with a monitoring well.
Standard Error [parameter] — The measure of variability or uncertainty in the expected discounted reward across different cases.
Discounted Return [parameter] — The cumulative reward over time, adjusted for the time value of money, in the context of surrogate model fidelity comparison.
Trap (MT) [geologicalbody] — A geological body used in the analysis, likely representing a trap in the context of CO2 storage and geological processes.
Free (MT) [geologicalbody] — A geological body used in the analysis, likely representing a free flow path in the context of CO2 storage and geological processes.
Exit (MT) [geologicalbody] — A geological body used in the analysis, likely representing an exit point in the context of CO2 storage and geological processes.
Seismic Saturation Observations [technology] — Techniques for observing the saturation of CO2 plumes using seismic surveys and spatial filtering with Gaussian kernel.
3D Example [geologicalbody] — A three-dimensional representation of the geological structure used in the example to demonstrate seismic observations in carbon storage POMDP.
Carbon Storage POMDP [technology] — A partially observable Markov decision process used for planning and decision-making in carbon storage operations, incorporating seismic observations.
Seismic Saturation Map [material] — A map depicting the saturation level of CO2 plumes in the geological structure, used for spatial filtering with Gaussian kernel.
Gaussian Kernel [technology] — A technology used for spatial filtering with a Gaussian kernel to mimic seismic saturation observations.
True Saturation Map [material] — A map representing the actual saturation of the reservoir.
FNO Neural Network [technology] — A neural network used as a surrogate flow simulator to predict multi-phase flow in porous media.
Surrogate Flow Simulator [technology] — A technology used to simulate multi-phase flow in porous media to aid in decision-making.
True Saturation [material] — The actual saturation of the reservoir, as determined by geological and laboratory measurements.

High-Fidelity Model [technology] — A high-accuracy model used for predicting multi-phase flow in porous media to improve decision quality.<SEP>A model with higher training data for more accurate simulation results.
Decision Quality [parameter] — The measure of the effectiveness and safety of the decisions made by the planning method.
U-fno [technology] — An enhanced Fourier Neural Operator-based deep-learning model for multiphase flow.

Porosity Map [parameter] — A map of porosity values in the state space.<SEP>The map of porosity values in the state space used for simulation.<SEP>A representation of the porosity distribution within an aquifer, used for belief updates in the context of CO2 storage.
State Space [parameter] — The space of possible states in the policy space, which includes porosity maps.
FNO Models [technology] — Neural network models used to train the gas saturation.
Relative Squared-Error Loss [other] — A loss function used to ensure effective gradient propagation during model training.
Partially Observable Monte Carlo Planning with Observation Widening [technology] — A tree search algorithm used for online decision-making in continuous state, action, and observation spaces.
POMCP [technology] — A state-of-the-art online planner used for solving POMDPs with continuous observation spaces, but struggled to handle belief collapse beyond the root node.
DESPOT [technology] — A state-of-the-art online planner used for solving POMDPs with continuous observation spaces, but struggled to handle belief collapse beyond the root node.
Ensemble-Based Inference Method [technology] — A computational method used for estimating state uncertainties, such as the ensemble Kalman filter and ensemble smoother.
CO2 Saturation History [parameter] — The historical record of CO2 saturation levels in the aquifer at various times, used for informing the belief update of porosity.

Observed CO2 Saturation History (d2) [parameter] — The recorded history of CO2 saturation levels at the monitoring well, used for updating the belief of porosity maps.
Emission Reduction Approaches [UNKNOWN] — Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) is a method used in mitigation portfolios and emission reduction approaches.
Proposed Approach [UNKNOWN] — The proposed approach demonstrates superior performance, resulting in a higher trapped CO2 compared to the expert policy.
12,000 Training Data [UNKNOWN] — The high-fidelity model is trained with 12,000 training data.

Ketton Limestone [geologicalbody] — A type of carbonate rock used in the study.<SEP>A type of limestone from Ketton, England<SEP>A type of limestone used in the study, which is oolithic in nature.<SEP>A type of rock used in a single-phase reactive flow experiment.<SEP>A type of rock unit, specifically a limestone used in the experiment.

Pore-Scale Flow Field [geologicalbody] — The flow field at the pore scale, created by the pore structure and fluid distribution.<SEP>The flow characteristics at the scale of individual pores in the rock.
Time-Resolved Micro-CT Imaging [technology] — A technique used to capture images over time.<SEP>A method used to capture images of the injection process over time.

Direct Numerical Simulation [technology] — A computational technique to simulate the behavior of the system.<SEP>A simulation technique used to model the injection process.
Carbonate Minerals [material] — Minerals that can react with CO2 to form an acidic aqueous phase
Flow-Field Heterogeneity [parameter] — Variability in pore-scale flow patterns
Reactive Transport [process] — Transport of reactive species within the reservoir
Remaining Hydrocarbons [material] — Hydrocarbons that remain in the pore space after production, affecting the reactive transport and dissolution processes.
CO2-Rich Fluids [material] — Fluids rich in CO2 that are predicted to behave in certain formations with remaining hydrocarbons.
Single-Phase Carbonate Systems [geologicalbody] — Carbonate systems where fluid transport is primarily driven by a single phase.
Surface Reaction [process] — The chemical reaction that occurs at the surface of minerals, competing with advection and molecular diffusion during dissolution.
Brine- Conducting Network [geologicalbody] — The network of connected pores and throats that allow brine to flow through the rock.
Oil Mobilisation or Displacement [process] — The movement or displacement of oil to open previously blocked pore throats.

Decane [material] — The oil phase selected for the study.<SEP>Decane was selected as the oil phase in the experiment.<SEP>A hydrocarbon liquid used in the experiment.<SEP>A hydrocarbon liquid used for injection.<SEP>A hydrocarbon compound.
Synthetic Brine [material] — A solution prepared by dissolving NaCl and KCl in deionized water.
Potassium Iodide [material] — A compound used to dope the synthetic brine for X-ray contrast during imaging.
Crude Oil [material] — Crude oil was continuously injected at a constant flow rate of 0.001 mL min⁻¹ for two weeks.
Decalin [material] — Decalin was used to flush the sample after the ageing process.<SEP>A hydrocarbon liquid used in the experiment.
Confined Porous Medium [geologicalbody] — A sample used in the experiment, consisting of a porous medium under confinement.
Flow Apparatus [technology] — A system used for fluid injection and production in the experiment.
Micro-CT Scanner [technology] — A device used for imaging the sample in the experiment.

Confined Core Holder [wellborecomponent] — A device used to hold the core sample during the experiment.
Bottom Inlet [wellborecomponent] — A component used for fluid injection in the experiment.

CO2-Saturated Brine [material] — A solution of CO2 dissolved in brine used for injection.<SEP>A solution of CO2 dissolved in brine.<SEP>A mixture of CO2 and brine used in the experiment.<SEP>A mixture of carbon dioxide and water used in the high-flow rate injection experiment.
Time-Lapse Micro-CT Scans [technology] — A series of images acquired over time to monitor the displacement process.

Reactive Injection [process] — The process of injecting CO2-saturated brine at a high flow rate to induce chemical reactions.<SEP>The process of injecting CO2-saturated brine to modify the flow field and establish preferential flow pathways.<SEP>A process involving the injection of reactive brine at high flow rates into the hydraulically accessible pore space.
Continuous Injection [process] — The process of injecting CO2-saturated brine into a core sample.

Oil-Saturated Scan [parameter] — A reference scan used in identifying oil.

Pe [parameter] — Péclet number, used to characterize the relative efficiency of solute mass transfer through advection compared to diffusion.<SEP>A dimensionless number representing the Peclet number, indicating the relative importance of advection to diffusion.

Da [parameter] — Damköhler number, used to quantify the ratio between the timescales of a chemical reaction and the mass transfer.<SEP>A dimensionless number representing the Damköhler number, indicating the relative importance of chemical reactions to transport processes.
rmineral [parameter] — Mineral reaction rate, used to calculate the Damköhler number.
Oil Distribution [geologicalbody] — The distribution of oil within the rock, which can be affected by the dissolution process.
Pore-Network Changes [geologicalbody] — The changes in the network of pores within the rock as a result of the dissolution and oil swelling processes.
Preferred Flow Pathways [geologicalbody] — The specific flow paths within the rock where preferential flow occurs, which can be influenced by the dissolution and oil swelling processes.
Pe–Da Regime [technology] — A regime or model that describes the relationship between pore throat size (Pe) and diffusivity (Da) in the context of reactive injection processes.
Effective Reaction Rate (reff) [parameter] — The rate at which mineral reactions occur in the rock, taking into account unresolved porosity and other factors.
Remaining-Oil Distribution [geologicalbody] — The distribution of oil in the rock after CO2-saturated brine injection, which is affected by the pore structure changes.

Pore-Enlargement Pathway [geologicalbody] — A specific pathway within the sample where pores progressively enlarge and coalesce to form a high-porosity channel.
Multiphase Flow Field [process] — The flow field involving multiple phases of fluid in the porous medium, which evolves as CO2-saturated brine is injected.
Effective Reaction Rate [parameter] — The measurable quantity that describes the rate at which the chemical reactions occur in the CO2-saturated brine injection process.
Pore Enlargement [process] — A process involving the increase in size of the pores in the sample.
Porosity Profiles [parameter] — Axial porosity profiles that provide evidence for the structural evolution.

Preferential Channel [process] — A physical process involving the preferential pathway for dissolution and channel development.
Free CO2-Rich Phase [process] — A physical process indicating the formation of a CO2-rich phase near the sample inlet and within the developing channel.

Pore-Size Distribution [parameter] — A measurable quantity related to the size of the pores in the network, shifted towards larger radii.<SEP>A measurable quantity describing the distribution of pore sizes in the rock formation, shifted towards larger radii relative to the throat-size distribution.

Mean Coordination Number [parameter] — A measurable quantity related to the average coordination number of the pores in the network.<SEP>A measurable quantity describing the average number of connections each pore in the pore network has.<SEP>The mean coordination number (¯Z) of the pores.

Throat [geologicalbody] — A rock unit or structural feature in the context of geological storage, specifically referring to the throats connecting the pores in the rock.<SEP>A rock unit with a size and shape that can affect fluid flow and storage.<SEP>The narrow space between two adjacent pores.<SEP>The narrow channel connecting two pores in a porous medium.

Aspect Ratio [parameter] — The ratio of mean pore radius to mean throat radius, indicating the widening of constrictions controlling local hydraulic and capillary resistance.
Pore-Throat Enlargement [process] — The process of increasing the size of pore-throats in the rock.

Pore Radius [parameter] — A measurable quantity of the size of the pore through which fluid flows.

Reactive Surface Area [UNKNOWN] — Dissolution alters the reactive surface area

Remaining Oil [UNKNOWN] — Redistribution and enlargement of pore throats by remaining oil

Real-Options Valuation [process] — A site-specific valuation process that incorporates location-dependent characteristics into project cash flows under uncertainty.<SEP>The process of valuing real options under spatial heterogeneity and temporal uncertainty.

Technological Progress [parameter] — Uncertainties in the progress of technology.<SEP>Factors influencing the investment decision in the SRO model, including changes in carbon prices, fuel prices, operating conditions, and policy support.
Spatial Screening [process] — The process of identifying technically feasible locations for new CCUS-ready coal-fired power plants through national-scale spatial screening.

SRO Model [technology] — A model that evaluates the investment decision for a CCUS-ready coal power project under uncertainty, considering factors such as immediate investment, deferral, carbon prices, fuel prices, operating conditions, technological progress, and policy support.
CCUS-Ready Coal-fired Power Plants [geologicalbody] — Technically feasible sites for new CCUS-ready coal-fired power plants, evaluated based on five siting criteria on a 5 km × 5 km grid.
Technical Feasibility Sites [geologicalbody] — 194,027 technically feasible sites for new CCUS-ready coal-fired power plants, identified through national-scale spatial screening.
Operational Plants [geologicalbody] — Operational plants used in match rate calculations.
Proposed Plants [geologicalbody] — Proposed plants used in match rate calculations.
Operating Conditions [parameter] — Factors influencing the investment decision in the SRO model.
Policy Support [parameter] — Factors influencing the investment decision in the SRO model.
Spatial Real Options (SRO) Model [technology] — A model that evaluates each technically feasible site independently by combining stochastic simulation with an optimal-stopping procedure.

Monte Carlo Simulation [technology] — A method used to generate future trajectories of stochastic variables and estimate continuation values at each decision point.<SEP>A method used to obtain 10,000 realizations for Monte Carlo simulation with additional perturbed trajectories.
Least Squares Monte Carlo (LSMC) Method [technology] — A method used to estimate the continuation value at each decision point in the SRO model.
Source-Sink Relationships [parameter] — Site-specific source-sink relationships that are first incorporated into project cash flows before Monte Carlo simulation is used.

Project Cash Flows [parameter] — The cash flows simulated over a 35-year operating lifetime, evaluated under the corresponding market, technology, and policy conditions.<SEP>The financial outcomes of a project
Coal Power System [parameter] — A component of the annual project cash flow, representing the coal power system.<SEP>A system that generates electricity using coal as fuel.

CCUS System [parameter] — A component of the annual project cash flow, representing the carbon capture, utilization, and storage system.<SEP>A system that captures, utilizes, and stores carbon dioxide to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions.
Investment Year [parameter] — The year in which investment decisions are made, allowed between 2025 and 2060.
CO₂ Storage [geologicalbody] — Four options for CO₂ storage: enhanced oil recovery (EOR), enhanced gas recovery (EGR), enhanced coalbed methane (ECBM), and enhanced water recovery (EWR).
Oil Reservoir [geologicalbody] — A type of CO₂ storage option for enhanced oil recovery.
Gas Reservoir [geologicalbody] — A type of CO₂ storage option for enhanced gas recovery.
Coal Prices [parameter] — Stochastic uncertainty represented through coal prices.
Annual Generation Hours [parameter] — Stochastic uncertainty represented through annual generation hours.
Oil or Gas Prices [parameter] — Stochastic uncertainty represented through oil or gas prices.
Carbon Trading Revenue [parameter] — Revenue generated from carbon trading within the CCUS system.
Coal Plant [wellborecomponent] — A coal power system that generates electricity using coal as fuel.
35-Year Operating Lifetime [parameter] — The operating lifetime of a coal plant.
Original Oil Price Trajectory [parameter] — The original oil price trajectory sampled from the IPCC AR6 scenario database.
Original Scenario Trajectories [parameter] — The original 1,045 scenario trajectories retained in the simulation set.
Original Gas Price Trajectory [parameter] — The original gas price trajectory extracted from the IPCC AR6 scenario database.
Generation-Hour Subsidies [regulation] — A fiscal instrument in China's CCUS policy framework, providing generation-hour subsidies to support policy interventions.

Investment-Cost Subsidies [regulation] — A fiscal instrument in China's CCUS policy framework, providing investment-cost subsidies to support policy interventions.<SEP>Investment-cost subsidies are financial incentives provided to lower the cost of investment.

Policy Sensitivity Scenarios (SW1–SW8) [technology] — Scenarios established to evaluate the effectiveness of alternative policy designs, combining technology learning pathways with subsidy mechanisms.
Province-Specific Economic Data [parameter] — Economic data specific to each province used in the SRO framework to assess CCUS-ready coal power investment.
High-Resolution Geospatial Datasets [geologicalbody] — Geospatial datasets used in the SRO framework to represent both spatial heterogeneity and temporal uncertainty.
5 Km × 5 Km Spatial Grid [parameter] — A spatial grid used in the SRO framework to project geospatial and economic parameters.
Carbon Market Trading Price [parameter] — The price of carbon market trading set to the 2024 annual average of 68.15 yuan/t used as the starting point of the stochastic carbon-price process.
Provincial Coal Price Indices [parameter] — Official provincial coal price indices used to represent provincial coal prices in the SRO framework.
On-Grid Electricity Prices [parameter] — Electricity prices obtained from the official benchmark tariffs for coalfired electricity generation in each province.

Provincial Average Annual Generation Hours [parameter] — Average annual generation hours during 2015–2020 used to characterize initial operating conditions for projecting future generation under uncertain market environments.
Land-Use Constraints [geologicalbody] — Constraints derived from national geospatial datasets used in the SRO framework.
Terrain Conditions [geologicalbody] — Terrain information derived from national geospatial datasets used in the SRO framework.
CO₂ Source–Sink Matching Information [geologicalbody] — Information on CO₂ source-sink matching derived from national geospatial datasets used in the SRO framework.
Geological Storage Resource [geologicalbody] — A resource that can store geological fluids
CCUS-Ready Coal Power Projects [technology] — Coal power projects that are prepared for CCUS integration
Geospatial Information [parameter] — Information related to the location and spatial distribution of resources
Economic Parameters [parameter] — Economic variables used in the SRO framework
Policy Assumptions [parameter] — Assumptions about the policies affecting CCUS projects
CO2 Source-Sink Matching [parameter] — The process of matching CO2 sources with storage sinks
Investment Window [parameter] — The time period during which a project can be economically viable
CO2-EOR [process] — Enhanced oil recovery using CO2.<SEP>Enhanced Oil Recovery process using CO2<SEP>A process used in CO2-enhanced oil recovery.

Coal-seam Storage [geologicalbody] — Storage in coal seams<SEP>A method of storing CO2 in coal seams.
Generation-hour Compensation [parameter] — Compensation based on generation hours

Project Value [parameter] — The economic value of a project evaluated at the optimal investment timing.<SEP>The economic value of a CO2 storage project.<SEP>Project value represents the economic benefits of a project.

Investment-Cost Subsidy [technology] — A policy instrument used to promote CCUS-ready coal power investment by subsidizing investment costs.<SEP>A policy instrument used to incentivize CO2 storage projects.
Oil- and Gas-Reservoir Storage [geologicalbody] — A type of geological body where oil and gas are stored.
National Spatiotemporal Investment Maps [technology] — Maps that identify priority areas for CCUS deployment based on future uncertainty.
CO2 Pipeline Network Optimization [technology] — A method for optimizing the design and operation of CO2 pipeline networks.
Endogenous Capacity Expansion [process] — A process of increasing capacity within the system as a result of internal growth.
Site-Specific Geological Characterization [process] — A detailed process of characterizing the specific geological features of a site.
Deep Emissions Reductions [UNKNOWN] — CCUS is capable of delivering deep emissions reductions while preserving dispatchable capacity.
WellboreComponent [UNKNOWN] — Well is a wellbore component used for the injection and extraction of fluids such as CO2 in the CCUS process.
Stochastic Uncertainty [UNKNOWN] — Stochastic uncertainty represented through carbon prices.
Least Squares Monte Carlo Algorithm [UNKNOWN] — The Monte Carlo simulation is discretized and incorporated into the Least Squares Monte Carlo algorithm.
Technology Learning Pathways (P1 and P2) [UNKNOWN] — The scenarios combine these pathways with subsidy mechanisms to evaluate technological progress and policy incentives.
Subsidy Mechanisms [UNKNOWN] — The scenarios evaluate the impact of these mechanisms on optimal investment timing and project value.

Germany [geologicalbody] — A country used as a case study for the implementation of CO2 pipeline infrastructure.<SEP>The country in which the CO2 network topology is being designed and simulated.<SEP>Region covered by the network elevation distribution<SEP>A country used as a case study for future assessments of integrated CCUS infrastructure.
CO2 Pipeline Infrastructure [technology] — A network of pipelines designed to transport CO2, a key component in the study.<SEP>The infrastructure for transporting CO2 through pipelines.
Multiphysical Network Simulator MYNTS [technology] — A simulation tool used to assess the technical feasibility of the CO2 pipeline network.
Cement and Lime Production Sites [geologicalbody] — Existing sites for cement and lime production included in the study.
Waste Incineration Sites [geologicalbody] — Existing waste incineration sites included in the study.<SEP>Current locations of waste incineration sites.

Coastal CO2 Hubs [geologicalbody] — Four coastal CO2 hubs included in the study.
Border Crossing Points [geologicalbody] — Border crossing points included in the study.

Investment Costs [parameter] — The calculated investment costs for the optimized pipeline system, estimated to be about 17 billion Euros.<SEP>Estimated investment costs for the optimized pipeline system.

Pipeline Transport [process] — A method for transporting CO2 over long distances using pipelines, which explicitly accounts for elevation and possible impurities.<SEP>A transport mode focused on in the current study, characterized by higher operational expenditures but lower capital costs compared to other modes.
Mixed Normed Diameter [parameter] — A system of pipeline diameters consisting of DN700 on main corridors and DN500/DN400 on branches, designed to connect most sites.

Carbon Storage and Transport Act (KSpTG) [regulation] — A comprehensive legal framework for both the permanent storage of CO2 and the permitting and operation of CO2 pipelines in Germany.<SEP>A law enabling onshore storage for CO2.<SEP>A regulation enabling onshore storage in Germany.
CO2 Pipeline [technology] — A type of infrastructure used for the transport of CO2 through pipelines.
North Sea [geologicalbody] — A body of water where CO2 is stored primarily in geological formations.<SEP>The storage facilities in the North Sea to which CO2 is loaded from the ports.

CO2 Pipeline Network [technology] — A network for the transportation of CO2 through pipelines.<SEP>A network of pipelines designed for CO2 transport and storage.<SEP>A network designed for the transportation of CO2.
CO2 Capture, Transport, and Storage [process] — The process of capturing CO2, transporting it, and storing it.
National Carbon Management Strategy [technology] — A national strategy for managing carbon, likely involving CO2 capture, transport, and storage.
Energy System Studies [process] — Studies on energy systems that include aspects of CO2 pipeline infrastructure.
European CO2 Pipeline System [process] — A potential European system for transporting CO2 through pipelines.

Straight-Line Connections [process] — A method for developing the topology of CO2 pipeline networks by assuming straight lines between sources and sinks.<SEP>A method for connecting sources and sinks in CO2 pipeline networks using straight lines.

Flexible Routing Methods [process] — A method for developing the topology of CO2 pipeline networks that allows for more flexible routing.<SEP>Methods for routing CO2 through pipelines in a flexible and adaptable manner.

Climate-Neutral Energy System [technology] — A system designed to be carbon-neutral, focusing on CO2 capture, utilization, and storage.<SEP>A proposed energy system in Germany aimed at reducing carbon emissions and achieving climate neutrality.
Pressure Calculations [technology] — Methods for determining the pressure levels necessary for CO2 transportation in pipelines.
Pump Placement [technology] — Strategies for placing pumps in CO2 pipeline networks to ensure efficient transport.

Waste Incineration [process] — A process where waste is burned to produce heat and energy, generating CO2 emissions.<SEP>A method for processing waste to produce energy.<SEP>A process from which CO2 is captured for the study.
Existing Natural Gas Transmission Pipelines [technology] — Pipelines used for the transmission of natural gas that are also repurposed for CO2 transport.
Elegancy Project [technology] — A project that combines CO2 pipeline networks with simplified pressure and pump placement calculations.
JRC Study [technology] — A study conducted by JRC that uses straight-line connections to aggregate various locations and includes a ramp-up analysis of CO2 infrastructure.
Austria Study [technology] — A study developed jointly with a network operator in Austria, including pressure calculations and pump placement.

CO2 Network Topology [process] — A network topology designed for CO2 transport in Germany, including locations of CO2 sources and sinks and potential transport routes for CO2 from neighboring countries.
Pipeline [geologicalbody] — Pipelines used for transporting CO2 in the network topology.<SEP>A structure for transporting CO2.

MYNTS [technology] — A pipeline planning tool used to calculate system parameters like the diameter of pipelines and the need for pumps and compressors.<SEP>A software designed to plan, simulate, and optimize energy networks across various sectors.<SEP>A software tool that solves non-isothermal 1D steady-state pipeline flow equations using a semi-coupled approach.<SEP>A reservoir simulation tool<SEP>A simulation tool

Pump [technology] — Pumps used in the CO2 transport network.<SEP>Devices used to increase the pressure of CO2 in the pipeline network, especially after long stretches or at major elevation changes.<SEP>A component used in the CO2 transport network to move fluid and potentially control temperature<SEP>A device that maintains a constant inlet pressure of 170 barg at the downstream end of the route.
Compressor [wellborecomponent] — Compressors used in the CO2 transport network.
Scenario [process] — A hypothetical situation used to test and validate the method, defined based on different assumptions about CO2 transit, capture, and utilization volumes.

CO2 Pipeline Topology [process] — A physical simulation describing the algorithm for the physical CO2 flow modeling and the design of specific system components.<SEP>The overall layout and design of CO2 transport pipelines derived from potential CO2 sources and sinks.<SEP>A network design for CO2 transport pipelines with high spatial resolution.

German-Wide Pipeline System [geologicalbody] — A network of pipelines connecting individual points within Germany, aiming to transport CO2 at least distances following existing gas pipeline corridors.

Industry Decarbonisation Scenario [scenario] — A consistent industry decarbonisation scenario developed for the research project 'Langfristszenarien III', calculated for the German Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Protection (BMWK).
O45-H2 Scenario [scenario] — A scenario that aims to achieve climate neutrality in Germany by 2045, utilizing hydrogen-based processes as key decarbonization strategy.
CO2 Capture (CC) [technology] — A process applied to hard-to-abate sectors that lack alternative abatement options, focusing on cement and lime production and waste incineration.
Carbon Capture and Utilisation (CCU) [technology] — A method for producing basic chemicals such as olefins & aromatics, methanol, and urea from captured CO2.
Offshore Geological CO2 Storage [geologicalbody] — A method for storing CO2 under the North Sea, part of the scenario for achieving climate neutrality in Germany.
KSpTG [regulation] — Germany’s Carbon Transport and Storage Law, in line with recent political discussions.<SEP>A regulation enabling onshore storage in Germany.
Wilhelmshaven [geologicalbody] — A port being considered for the installation of CO2 terminals for loading ships.
Bremerhaven [geologicalbody] — A port being considered for the installation of CO2 terminals for loading ships.
Brunsb{"u}ttl [geologicalbody] — A port being considered for the installation of CO2 terminals for loading ships.
Rostock [geologicalbody] — A port being considered for the installation of CO2 terminals for loading ships.
Gas Border Crossing Points [geologicalbody] — Assumed border crossing points for the import and export of CO2 from and to neighboring countries.
HtA+CCU [scenario] — A scenario where CO2 demand is 31 Mt in 2045, with 27 Mt required for methanol production.

HtA+Imports [scenario] — A scenario where CO2 demand is significantly larger in 2045, including emissions from cement, lime, waste incineration, and neighboring countries.<SEP>A case with a relatively high transport volume of CO2
2045 [parameter] — The year in which the CO2 demand and emissions are calculated.
CO2 Hubs [technology] — Four CO2 hubs used to transport emissions to storage sites under the North Sea.<SEP>Locations for sequestration of CO2.
Dense-Phase CO2 Transport Pipeline [process] — A type of CO2 transport pipeline that allows higher transport volumes than gas-phase CO2 transport, making it preferred for long-distance pipelines.

Natural Gas Transmission Network Pipeline [wellborecomponent] — Pipelines used for the transmission of natural gas, which are considered for conversion to CO2 transport pipelines.<SEP>A network of pipelines used for the transmission of natural gas, which is utilized for CO2 transportation.
CO2 Grid [technology] — A proposed network for transporting CO2 via natural gas transmission network pipelines.
CO2 Sinks [other] — Current refinery and chemical sites as well as CO2 hubs for sequestration.
Lime Locations [other] — Current locations of lime production sites.
Cement Locations [other] — Current locations of cement production sites.
German National CO2 Infrastructure Network [geologicalbody] — A national CO2 infrastructure network.

Specific Enthalpy [material] — A measurable quantity representing the specific enthalpy of the fluid, defined as H = e + P/ρ, where e is the specific energy and ρ is the density of the fluid.<SEP>The specific enthalpy (H) is defined as the sum of the specific energy (e) and the product of pressure (P) and density (ρ), where e represents the specific energy, and ch is the heat transfer coefficient.
Dynamic Viscosity [material] — A measurable quantity representing the dynamic viscosity of the fluid, denoted as µvisc.<SEP>A measurable quantity denoting the dynamic viscosity of the fluid.
Reynolds Number [parameter] — A measurable quantity representing the Reynolds number, denoted as Re, calculated as Re = 4|Qm|/(πµviscD).
Mass Flow [parameter] — A measurable quantity representing the mass flow, denoted as Qm, calculated as Qm = ρvπD2/4.
Dimensionless Friction Coefficient [parameter] — A measurable quantity representing the dimensionless friction coefficient, denoted as λ(k/D, Re), using the Nikuradse formula or the Hofer formula.
Pipe Roughness [parameter] — A measurable quantity representing the pipe's roughness, denoted as k.<SEP>A measurable quantity denoting the roughness of the pipe.

Heat Transfer Coefficient [parameter] — A measurable quantity representing the heat transfer coefficient, denoted as ch.<SEP>The heat transfer coefficient (ch) is a parameter in the equation H = e + P/ρ, where e represents the specific energy, and H is the specific enthalpy.<SEP>A measurable quantity denoting the heat transfer coefficient.

Soil Temperature [parameter] — A measurable quantity representing the soil temperature, denoted as Ts.<SEP>The soil temperature (Ts) is a parameter in the equation dT = µJT dP, where µJT is the Joule-Thomson coefficient.<SEP>A measurable quantity denoting the temperature of the soil.
Specific Enthalpy Equation [process] — A physical process representing the specific enthalpy of the fluid, defined as H = e + P/ρ, where e is the specific energy and ρ is the density of the fluid.
Dimension Equation [process] — A physical process representing the dimension equation, defined as dP/dx = -λ(2Dρv2 - ρv dv/dx - ρg dh/dx).
Temperature Equation [process] — A physical process representing the temperature equation, defined as dH/dx = -πDch(T - Ts).
Joule-Thomson Coefficient [parameter] — The Joule-Thomson coefficient (µJT) is defined as µJT = (−∂H/∂P)T /(∂H/∂T)P, where H is the specific enthalpy, P is the pressure, and T is the temperature.
Kirchhoffs Laws [technology] — Kirchhoff’s laws are used for connecting the components of the network, such as pipes, pumps, regulators, valves, heaters, and coolers.
MYNTS Software [technology] — MYNTS is a software used for solving non-isothermal 1D steady-state pipeline flow equations, incorporating the equations for enthalpy and gas composition.
Semi-Coupled Approach [technology] — MYNTS employs a semi-coupled approach, iterating the equations for enthalpy and gas composition alongside the pipeline flow equations.

1D Steady-State Pipeline Flow Equations [process] — The 1D steady-state pipeline flow equations are used in modeling gas transport networks and their components, including regulators, pumps, heaters, and coolers.
Non-Isothermal 1D Steady-State Pipeline Flow Equations [process] — Equations used in the MYNTS software to model flow in pipelines under non-isothermal conditions.
Gas Composition [parameter] — The proportion of different gases in a mixture, represented by the vector of mole fractions (ζ) in the software.
Molar Density (ρm) [parameter] — The mass of a substance per unit volume, calculated by the software.
Compressibility Factor (z) [parameter] — A dimensionless ratio that indicates how much a gas can be compressed by pressure and temperature changes.
Height (h) [parameter] — A height-related parameter computed by the software.
MYNTS 4.9.5 [technology] — A software tool used for the simulations.
Pipe Diameter [parameter] — A measurable quantity denoting the diameter of the pipe.
Total Pipe Length [parameter] — A measurable quantity denoting the total length of the pipe.
Nodal Height [parameter] — A measurable quantity denoting the height of the terrain.
Molar Mass [parameter] — A measurable quantity denoting the molar mass of the fluid.
Fluid Composition [parameter] — A measurable quantity denoting the composition of the fluid.
Setpoint Pressure [parameter] — A measurable quantity denoting the setpoint pressure.

DN500 [geologicalbody] — A standard diameter of the pipeline.<SEP>A standard diameter of pipeline used in the network design.<SEP>Diameter of the pipeline, which is 500 mm.<SEP>A specific diameter of pipeline used in the network, indicating the inner diameter of 500 mm.<SEP>A pipeline diameter used in the CO2 network, either uniformly or in hybrid configurations.

DN700 [geologicalbody] — A standard diameter of the pipeline.<SEP>A standard diameter of pipeline used in the network design.<SEP>Diameter of the pipeline, which is 700 mm.<SEP>A specific diameter of pipeline used in the network, indicating the inner diameter of 700 mm.<SEP>A pipeline diameter used in high-flow backbone segments of the CO2 network.

DN900 [geologicalbody] — A standard diameter of the pipeline.<SEP>A standard diameter of pipeline used in the network design, though not considered realistic under current industry practice.<SEP>Diameter of the pipeline, which is 900 mm.<SEP>A specific diameter of pipeline used in the network, indicating the inner diameter of 900 mm.

DN400 [parameter] — Diameter of the pipeline, which is 400 mm.<SEP>A specific diameter of pipeline used in the network, indicating the inner diameter of 400 mm.<SEP>A pipeline diameter used in low-flow branches of the CO2 network.
CO2 Network Feasibility Study for Austria [regulation] — A study conducted by the CO2 Network for Austria, providing cost estimates for CO2 pipeline infrastructure.

Rhineland-Palatinate and Hesse [geologicalbody] — Border regions where the CO2 flow divides.
Hamburg Region [geologicalbody] — Region where the CO2 flow branches merge again.
CO2 Network [geologicalbody] — Network of pipelines and pumps for CO2 transport.

Pumps [technology] — Pumps placed at locations where pressure recovery is required.<SEP>Equipment used to control the flow in the pipeline section.<SEP>Devices used to ensure safe operation in dense phase
Pumping Stations [wellborecomponent] — Locations where pumps are installed to ensure reliable CO2 transport.
85 Barg [parameter] — The minimum operating pressure of the CO2 transport network.
Cooling [process] — The process of reducing the temperature of CO2 after it has been compressed
Phase Diagram [technology] — A diagram showing the pressure-temperature distribution of CO2 in the network nodes
Phase Curve [geologicalbody] — Pink curve representing the boundary between gaseous and dense phases in the phase diagram

Elevation Differences [parameter] — Elevation changes between locations where CO2 is produced and transported<SEP>Terrain height variations affecting pressure distribution in dense-phase CO2 networks.

Fluid [material] — CO2 in its dense phase
Terrain Elevation [parameter] — The elevation of the terrain in meters.<SEP>A measurable quantity such as terrain elevation in the pipeline section.

O2 [material] — Oxygen<SEP>A chemical species admixed at up to 4% in the CO2 network.
MINTH [technology] — A technology used for physical pipeline simulation
Energy System Scenario Data [parameter] — Data used for the future CO2 pipeline systems assessment
Langfristzenarien III [parameter] — Energy system scenario data used in the study

Onshore Storage Projects [technology] — Projects aimed at storing CO2 on land.
European Scale [parameter] — The scale at which storage capacities are to be assessed.

Dense-Phase Pipeline [technology] — A pipeline used for transporting CO2 in a dense phase

Routing [process] — The process of determining the path for CO2 pipeline routes
Natural Gas Network [geologicalbody] — An existing network of pipelines used for transporting natural gas

Elevation Changes [parameter] — The changes in elevation along the pipeline route, affecting energy consumption

SimCCS [technology] — A technology used in related work, where the model for CO2 transport has been simplified to integrate it into the optimization task.<SEP>A physical simulation tool used to predict the behavior of the transported fluid in the network planning.
Ship [technology] — An alternative transport mode, particularly attractive for small to medium transport volumes and for flexible or temporary connections.
Rail [technology] — An alternative transport mode, particularly attractive for small to medium transport volumes and for flexible or temporary connections.
Europe [geologicalbody] — A continent used as a context for future assessments of integrated CCUS infrastructure.
DN700 Pipelines [wellborecomponent] — A type of pipeline used in the high-flow backbone segments of the CO2 transport network.
DN500 Pipelines [wellborecomponent] — A type of pipeline used in the low-flow branches of the CO2 transport network.
DN400 Pipelines [wellborecomponent] — A type of pipeline used in the low-flow branches of the CO2 transport network.

Equipment [parameter] — Equipment affected by pressure variations and terrain height in the CO2 network.

HtA+Imports.csv [material] — A CSV file containing CO2 quantities used per location.

Private and Public Project Developers [UNKNOWN] — The act leaves the development of CO2 pipeline infrastructure initially to private and public project developers, with access and connection rules defined at the network level.
Literature on CO2 Pipeline Networks [UNKNOWN] — There is an increasing body of literature on CO2 pipeline networks in Europe.
Topology Development [UNKNOWN] — Some studies assume straight-line connections between sources and sinks for topology development.

Climate Neutrality in Germany [UNKNOWN] — The O45-H2 scenario aims to achieve climate neutrality in Germany by 2045 through the utilization of hydrogen-based processes as key decarbonization strategies.
Pipes [UNKNOWN] — Kirchhoff’s laws are used for connecting the components of the network, such as pipes, pumps, regulators, valves, heaters, and coolers.
Valves [UNKNOWN] — Kirchhoff’s laws are used for connecting the components of the network, such as pipes, pumps, regulators, valves, heaters, and coolers.
Heaters [UNKNOWN] — Kirchhoff’s laws are used for connecting the components of the network, such as pipes, pumps, regulators, valves, heaters, and coolers.
Coolers [UNKNOWN] — Kirchhoff’s laws are used for connecting the components of the network, such as pipes, pumps, regulators, valves, heaters, and coolers.
Main Pipelines [UNKNOWN] — DN700 pipelines are used along the main pipelines where the mass flow rates are highest and pressure losses would be significant.

Integrated Approach [UNKNOWN] — The integrated approach is used for modeling CO2 transport systems.

Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) [process] — A set of technologies and practices aimed at capturing carbon dioxide from industrial sources, utilizing it, and storing it in a manner that prevents its release into the atmosphere.

Digital Rock Physics [technology] — A computational framework used for understanding the physical properties of porous rocks, particularly in the context of permeability upscaling.<SEP>A computational approach used to simulate and analyze the behavior of rocks at the microscale, which can provide insights into their macroscopic properties.
Permeability Characterization [process] — The process of determining the capacity of porous formations to conduct fluids.

Core Scale [parameter] — The scale at which permeability is assessed using core-scale, low-resolution CT images, which represent larger rock samples.<SEP>A larger length scale used in permeability estimation, focusing on core samples.<SEP>The scale at which permeability maps are predicted using the trained CNN in the workflow.
Sub-Core Volumes [parameter] — Smaller volumes of rock within a larger core sample used for permeability prediction.

Permeability Upscaling [process] — The process of determining the upscaled permeability at the core scale through a Darcy flow solver based on the predicted sub-core permeability map, which balances computational efficiency and prediction accuracy.
Sub-Core Volume Size [parameter] — The optimal sub-core volume size that balances computational efficiency and prediction accuracy in the permeability upscaling process.
Pore Structure Heterogeneity [parameter] — The variation in the structure of pores across a wide range of length scales, leading to scale-dependent permeability.
Micrometer-Scale Pores [geologicalbody] — Pores with a size on the micrometer scale, contributing to the overall permeability at the core scale.
Centimeter-Scale Cores [geologicalbody] — Cores with a size on the centimeter scale, used for permeability upscaling from micrometer-scale pores.
Scale-Dependent Permeability [process] — A phenomenon where permeability values vary significantly at different length scales due to the heterogeneity and anisotropy of the porous medium.
Pore Scale [parameter] — The smallest length scale used in permeability estimation, focusing on individual pores.
Field Scale [parameter] — An even larger length scale used in permeability estimation, focusing on the entire field.
Upscaling Methods [technology] — Methods and models used to improve large-scale permeability estimations based on small-scale data while maintaining geological consistency.
Nonnegative Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (NPOD) [technology] — A model used in conjunction with Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) to upscale permeability.
Interpolation Algorithms [technology] — Algorithms used to interpolate permeability values between different scales.
Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) [technology] — A novel analytical approach integrated with upscaling methods to achieve rapid permeability upscaling from pore to core scale.
Convolutional Long-Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM) [technology] — A component of a hybrid deep learning framework used to upscale permeability from pore-scale to core-scale systems.
Particle Swarm Optimization [technology] — A component of a hybrid deep learning framework used to upscale permeability from pore-scale to core-scale systems.
Fast Marching Method [technology] — A component of a hybrid deep learning framework used to upscale permeability from pore-scale to core-scale systems.
Graph Theory-Based Techniques [technology] — A method used to upscale permeability from dynamic pore-scale models to Darcy-scale representations.
Minkowski Functionals [technology] — A tool used for rock type classification in permeability upscaling.<SEP>Mathematical tools used for rock type classification.
Support Vector Machines (SVM) [technology] — A model used in conjunction with Minkowski functionals for permeability upscaling from 3D pore-scale models to larger-scale rock.
Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM) [technology] — A model used in conjunction with Minkowski functionals for permeability upscaling from 3D pore-scale models to larger-scale rock.
Dynamic Pore-scale Models [process] — Models that simulate the flow properties at the smallest scale of pores.
Darcy-scale Representations [process] — Representations of permeability at a larger scale than the pore scale.
Mishra et al. [other] — Authors of a study utilizing graph theory-based techniques to upscale permeability.
Jiang et al. [other] — Authors of a study incorporating Minkowski functionals for rock type classification.
High-resolution CT Images [material] — Images with high spatial resolution used to calculate reliable permeability data.
Lattice Boltzmann Method [technology] — A computational fluid dynamics method used to model complex geometries and multiphase flows.
Tsuji et al. [other] — Authors of studies using the Lattice Boltzmann Method for permeability estimation.
Jiang and Tsuji [other] — Authors of studies using the Lattice Boltzmann Method for permeability estimation.
Wang et al. [other] — Authors of a study using high-resolution CT images for permeability estimation.
Suss et al. [other] — Authors of studies using high-resolution CT images for permeability estimation.
Li et al. [other] — Authors of a study using high-resolution CT images for permeability estimation.

High-Resolution CT Images [technology] — High-resolution CT imaging technology used to facilitate precise calculations of rock properties.<SEP>CT images with higher resolution from which small subvolumes were extracted for permeability determination.<SEP>CT images with high spatial resolution used for accurate pore-scale flow simulation.

Low-Resolution CT Images [technology] — Low-resolution CT imaging technology used to provide coverage over larger sample volumes.<SEP>CT images with lower resolution used in the study for permeability prediction.
Permeability Uscalping [process] — The process of upscaling permeability by integrating high-precision data from high-resolution CT images with broader-scale data from low-resolution CT images.

3D Digital Rock Models [technology] — 3D digital rock models used to predict characteristics such as 3D flow fields, capillary pressure, permeability, and relative permeability.<SEP>Models used for predicting relative permeability and capillary pressure.

3D CNN [technology] — 3D Convolutional Neural Network used to predict relative permeability and capillary pressure from 3D images of digital sandstones.<SEP>A deep learning model used for predicting relative permeability and capillary pressure from 3D images of digital sandstones.
3D Flow Fields [process] — 3D flow fields predicted using 3D digital rock models.
U-Net Architecture CNN [technology] — A deep learning model used for predicting 3D velocity field and permeability from 3D binary images of reticulated foam.
3D Digital Rock Images [material] — 3D images used as input for deep learning models to predict relative permeability and capillary pressure.
Physics-informed Machine Learning [technology] — A method used for predicting relative permeability and capillary pressure by combining physics-informed machine learning and reinforcement learning.
Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM) [technology] — A method used to determine permeability values of small subvolumes extracted from high-resolution CT images.
Boise Sandstone Core [geologicalbody] — A core sample used in the study due to its extensive characterization of grain-size distribution, pore structure, and petrophysical properties.
Jiang et al. (2023) [regulation] — A workflow proposed by Jiang et al. in 2023 for permeability upscaling modeling.
Louis et al. (2024) [regulation] — A study evaluating the permeability upscaling modeling of Boise sandstone cores.

Boise Sandstone [geologicalbody] — A type of sandstone with a dominant grain size of around 100 µm, as measured from thin section optical images.<SEP>A type of sedimentary rock, specifically sandstone found in Boise, used as a reference material.<SEP>A type of rock with small pore sizes, used in the study.
Xradia Versa XRM-500 [technology] — A micro-CT scanner used for micro X-ray CT imaging of rock samples at two resolutions: 20µm/voxel (coarse) and 3µm/voxel (fine).

LBM Flow Solver [technology] — A computational fluid dynamics solver used to obtain rock permeability data from binarized high-resolution CT images.<SEP>A solver used for calculating permeability properties of high-resolution subvolumes.<SEP>A computational method used to simulate single-phase flow in the z-direction to calculate permeability.
Low-Resolution CT Image [material] — A low-resolution CT image used for scanning the entire rock core.

High-Resolution CT Image [material] — A high-resolution CT image used for scanning the center core region at the pore scale.<SEP>Imaging technique used to capture detailed information about the pore structure.
Permeability Dataset [parameter] — A dataset containing permeability values calculated from high-resolution micro-CT images.
High-Resolution Subvolumes [geologicalbody] — Extracted subvolumes from the segmented high-resolution micro-CT images.
Low-Resolution Subvolumes [geologicalbody] — Subvolumes in the coarse-scanned 3D CT raw images.
White Grids [geologicalbody] — Subvolumes extracted from the outer region of the large-scale rock sample in low-resolution CT images.
Predicted Permeability Map [parameter] — A map of permeability predicted by the trained CNN model.
Micro-CT Images [geologicalbody] — High-resolution CT images used for pore-scale flow direct numerical simulation.
Threshold Algorithm [technology] — A method based on the grayscale histogram of images to segment the pore and solid phases.
Solid Phases [geologicalbody] — The non-pore parts of the rock matrix.

Subvolumes [geologicalbody] — Parts of the reconstructed binarized pore-geometry model with specific dimensions for permeability calculation.<SEP>Subvolumes used for permeability and porosity calculations, with dimensions of 153, 313, and 463 voxels.<SEP>Divisions of a larger sample for analysis, each of a specific size.<SEP>Small sections of the porous medium used for analysis.
Micro-CT Image Processing [process] — The process of enhancing image quality and segmenting pore and solid phases in high-resolution CT images.

CT Images [material] — High-resolution and low-resolution CT images used for permeability and porosity calculations.<SEP>Computed tomography images used to observe the internal structure of rock cores.<SEP>Raw computed tomography images used to observe rock structure and predict permeability, showing density variations corresponding to permeability variations.<SEP>Computed tomography imaging technology used to visualize

Subvolume [geologicalbody] — A portion of rock analyzed for its structural and representativeness properties.<SEP>A portion of the rock or material used for training and prediction.<SEP>A defined region within the core for permeability and pressure measurements.<SEP>A portion of the porous media with a defined size used for permeability calculations.

Pore Network Modeling (PNM) [technology] — A method used to analyze the pore structure and connectivity of rock samples.<SEP>A method used to estimate the permeability of porous media by simplifying the complex microstructure into a network of interconnected nodes and edges.
Coordination Number [parameter] — A key topological property that reflects the average number of connections (throats) per pore body, indicating flow connectivity.
Standard Deviation of Permeability [parameter] — The measure of variability in permeability distribution for subvolumes.
Subvolume Size [parameter] — The size of subvolumes used in permeability prediction studies.<SEP>The size of the subvolume in CT images used for permeability prediction.
Data Diversity [parameter] — Variability in data due to local heterogeneities in the rock.
Outlier Subvolumes [parameter] — Subvolumes that are completely composed of flow paths or minerals.
Training Data [parameter] — The data used to train the deep learning model.

Kozeny-Carman (KC) Model [technology] — A classical model to describe the relationship between permeability and porosity.<SEP>A classical empirical model used to describe the relationship between permeability and porosity.<SEP>A traditional empirical model used for predicting permeability-porosity relationships.
100-Sized Subvolumes [parameter] — A specific size of subvolumes used in the study.
200-Sized Subvolumes [parameter] — A specific size of subvolumes used in the study.
300-Sized Subvolumes [parameter] — A specific size of subvolumes used in the study.
Kc Model [technology] — A model that only correlates permeability with porosity, neglecting the influence of pore microstructure and flow path connectivity.

CT Rock Model [material] — A model of rock structure captured by a CT scan used for comparison.<SEP>A computed tomography (CT) model of the rock sample, providing a detailed visualization of the rock's internal structure.

Rectangular Cuboid Regions [geologicalbody] — Three-dimensional regions with grid sizes of 42×42×267, 20×20×130, and 14×14×88, extracted from the same region of the CT scan for computational analysis.
Rectangular Cuboid Region [geologicalbody] — The computational domain used in the Darcy flow solver with specific grid sizes.
Core Sample [geologicalbody] — The physical sample used in the permeability and pressure distribution study.
Pressure Difference Map [parameter] — Maps showing the pressure differences between different cases.
Inlet [geologicalbody] — The start point of the flow in the porous medium.
Flow [process] — A physical process involving the movement of fluids through porous media.
Pore Network Modeling [technology] — A method used to simplify the complex microstructure of porous media by representing the pore space as a network of interconnected nodes and edges.
Pore Geometries [geologicalbody] — The geometric properties of the pores within the rock matrix.
Pressure Gradient Boundary Condition [parameter] — A condition applied along the flow direction to drive fluid movement in the pore network model.
Coreflooding Experiment [process] — An experimental method to measure the permeability of the entire core.
Coreflooding Experiment Data [material] — Data obtained from coreflooding experiments used to measure permeability.
PNM (Pore Network Model) [technology] — A method for modeling pore space using simplified geometries.
Deep-Learning-Based Method [technology] — A computational method used to obtain permeability data.
PNM [technology] — Pore Network Model used for reconstructing pore network from high-resolution CT images.
Darcy Flow Simulation [process] — Simulation technique used to model fluid flow through porous media under the influence of pressure gradients.
Arithmetic Average Permeability [parameter] — Average permeability calculated by taking the arithmetic mean of permeability values in subvolumes.
Deep Learning-Based Workflow [technology] — A method for predicting the upscaled absolute permeability of large rock cores using low-resolution CT images and deep learning.
Rock Cores [geologicalbody] — Rock samples used in permeability and porosity studies.

Machine Learning-Based Workflow [technology] — A method that integrates high-resolution flow data with low-resolution CT scans to predict permeability and upscale it from the millimeter-scale to the centimeter-scale, providing detailed pore structure information.
Crystalline Formations [geologicalbody] — Rock formations with high mineral content.
Metamorphic Formations [geologicalbody] — Rock formations that have undergone transformation due to heat and pressure.
Electrical Conductivity [parameter] — Measure of a rock's ability to conduct electric current.
Seismic Wave Velocities [parameter] — Measure of the speed at which seismic waves travel through a rock.
Mineralogical Properties [parameter] — Chemical and physical properties of minerals within a rock.
Chemical Properties [parameter] — Chemical composition of a rock.

Darcy Flow Solver [technology] — Darcy Flow Solver is a computational method used to calculate the upscaled permeability of the entire core, which is based on the predicted permeability map at the core scale. This tool is utilized to solve fluid flow equations in porous media and to compute the flow flux distribution in permeability maps.
